A plaque: 'DINING BALCONY — PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE GULLS, THEY ARE UNIONISED.'

interactables.name: Dorcas Wickerby (back from Gok'Gok Harbor)
pages: 'I took the ferry to Gok'Gok Harbor last week. Cogskill Arcade is all brass and steam and cryston lights. I've never been anywhere loud on purpose before.'
'Toggletec Emporium sells a toaster that writes you a poem. I bought one. The poems are bad. I love it more than I've loved most people.'
'Their Cryst-o-Games shop has cabinets that light up. I lost every copper I'd brought. Nan paid for the ferry for my birthday, so I've told her it went on soup.'
'Next I want to go to Tritone. Nan says not while there's fighting. I say they're playing music in the streets. We're both right, which is very annoying.'

interactables.name: Philippa Saltmarsh (gull watcher)
pages: 'That gull is Brian. That one's Brian too. The first Brian stole my sandwich two hundred years ago, and I've never had the heart to start a new list.'
'Best seat in Banañon Town, this. Every ship in the world comes through the strait, and not one of them can see your lunch from out there.'
She whistles two low notes and a gull drops onto the rail beside her. 'I piloted ships through here for ninety years. Now I just tell the Brians which ones are late.'

4: 'I knitted the Brians Selunemas hats. Eleven hats, nine Brians who'd wear them, and one Brian who ate his. In gull, that's a compliment.'

interactables.name: Gideon Brightwater (on a date)
pages: 'First date. I picked the balcony. Romantic, right? She's been holding the railing for twenty minutes. Is that good?'
'Should I take her down the chute? Is the chute romantic? My mum met my dad in a ferry queue and she still calls that romantic, so the bar is low.'
'I'm a ledger clerk at the cryston depot. I don't get out much. I practised this on my cat for a week, and she left halfway through every time.'

interactables.name: Tobias Wavecrest (balcony waiter)
pages: 'Table for one? Table for the view? Every table is for the view. Sit anywhere. Sit carefully.'
'Wavecrest is me; I'm Tobias of the Wavecrests. Wait, no — we do it the other way. Wavecrest Tobias. I always get that wrong on land.'
'Tip: order soup on a calm day. On a windy day, order soup and a raincoat.'
'Six generations of my family fished this strait. I'm the first who brings the fish to the table instead of out of the water. My mother finds that funnier than I do.'
brushoffs: 'Same table, same gossip, I'm afraid. The wind hasn't brought any more.'
'I've got soup going cold on three tables and a gull eyeing table nine, friend.'
'If you're not ordering, the gulls would like your seat.'

interactables.name: Duchess Marmalade (sunbathing)
pages: Duchess Marmalade is stretched out on the warmest plank of the Dining Balcony, the whole strait glittering behind her.
She lets you sit beside her. For a long moment you both just watch the ships. Then she leaves one perfect orange whisker on your sleeve. Lucky.
(You've followed the mall cat through every floor. Mall legend says her whisker is good luck in the arena. Mall legend is a cat.)
lockedPages: A warm, cat-shaped patch of sun on the planks. No cat. The cat is elsewhere. The cat is always elsewhere.

hidden.hint: That warm patch of sun on the planks has whiskers.

interactables.name: Balcony Planter
pages: A planter of sea-pinks clinging on in the wind. A little card: 'WE ARE VERY BRAVE FLOWERS.'

4: The sea-pinks are wrapped in Selunemas lights. A paper moon dangles over them.
5: The sea-pinks are wrapped in Selunemas lights. A paper moon dangles over them, and a tiny paper D'fain.

interactables.name: Dining Balcony Sign
pages: DINING BALCONY — OPEN-AIR DECK OVER THE ABSULINAUGHT STRAIT. Cliff stairs up to the arena at the south end.

interactables.name: Old Barnaby Squeezebox (busker)
pages: A mole with an accordion plays a sea shanty. 'Requests? I know four songs. Three are this one. The fourth was my wife's, and I don't play it out here.'
'Had the bandstand on Level One twenty-two years. Then the jingle machines came. They don't need lunch, or a stool, or paying. I've got the balcony now. Better wind.'
'That jingle box by the food court writes a song every nine minutes. I've been working on this shanty for nine years. It's nearly done.'

interactables.name: MALL BRAWL Poster
pages: A Goolax poster: a fist holding a foam finger holding a fist. 'MALL BRAWL 2026 — BRAWN & BRILLIANCE.'

1: A Goolax poster with a fresh sticker: 'TRYOUTS COMPLETE! THE GALLERIA TEAM IS SET!' Someone drew hearts around it.
2: A Goolax poster: 'NEXT: THE SLOOPERMARKET.' A cartoon sloop wears a shopping basket like a hat.
3: A Goolax poster: 'NEXT: PANTO.' A cartoon theatre mask is punching another theatre mask.
4: A Goolax poster: 'NEXT: MOFFIDGE.' Someone has drawn a D'fain beard on the fist.
5: A Goolax poster: 'FINAL CONTEST — SELUNEMAS — LOCATION: SECRET!' Someone has written 'the moon??' in pen.

interactables.name: Skeeton's Poster
pages: 'SKEETON'S: OFFICIAL OUTFITTER OF FEELING NICE.' A smaller sticker: 'NOT AN OFFICIAL GOOLAX SUPPLIER. YET.'

interactables.name: Goolax Banner
pages: GOOLAX MALL BRAWL — VISITING VENDORS EVERY WEEK AT THE S106 POP-UP BOOTHS! (All competitors welcome.)
Tiny print: 'Passes issued to competitors by the Goolax Competitor Liaison. Ask around!'

interactables.name: Leyline Tube
pages: A long glass tube runs along the back wall, glowing like a jellyfish. The brass hatch reads: 'ONE RIDER AT A TIME. NO SNACKS IN THE LEYLINE.'

interactables.name: Pemberton Burrowmere (Leyline Operator)
pages: Leyline Operator, at your service! I didn't dig this line. I found it, digging a well that fizzed. Then I dug round it. Next stop: Cogskill Arcade.
Fifty gold buys a round trip. Pay here on the way out; the ride home's free. Hop in the hatch, feet first, chin up.
Arrive a bit fizzy? That's the leyline saying hello. Shake it off before you shake anyone's hand.
Cogskill folk pop out of that tube blinking at all the sky. Then they ask where the food court is. It's DOWN, petal. Everything good here is down.
Forty years I dug wells round Banañon. There's a gnome at the Cogskill end; we tap messages down the line, morning and night. We've never met.
brushoffs: That's all the tube's brought up today, petal.
Rumours come up the line, not out of me. Wait for the next ride.
Mind the hatch on your way out. It's that way. Go on, petal.

interactables.name: Departures Board
pages: DEPARTURES: COGSKILL ARCADE, GOK'GOK HARBOR · ON TIME. Someone has chalked a little mushroom waving goodbye.

interactables.name: Gantry Bollworth (mall security)
pages: 'Gantry Bollworth, mall security. Twenty years on the Strait docks, then my back went. Now I mostly stop children licking the moss.'
'The new owners gave me a clipboard and a quota. Quota of what, it doesn't say. So I write down nice things people do. Page six is nearly full.'
'Brawlers, please, no practising in the Stem. Last week someone suplexed a planter, and I had to go and tell its gardener, and she cried.'
'My gran was a door-warden in a fae court, before they turned our lot out. She said you guard a door by being kind to whoever's on the wrong side of it.'

interactables.name: Pell Quarrystone (lamp-tender)
pages: 'Every glow-mushroom lamp in the rock is mine to tend. Two hundred and six. Two hundred and five if you don't count the shy one, and I'll not tell you which.'
'Down here the lamps are the sun. Folk forget that. The mushrooms don't. I came from the mine lamps at Glister thirty-one year ago and never went back up.'
He cups a dim cap and breathes on it, and it brightens like a cheek. 'Owners want timers. Click on, click off. A timer don't know when she's tired.'

interactables.name: Ines Thornbury (first visit)
pages: 'First time down here! I followed one smell, then a different smell, and now I'm lost in a very delicious way.'
'Is it true every stall is carved into the rock? Even the restrooms? ...Don't answer that.'
'I moved here from an orchard village a fortnight ago. Nobody back home has seen the sea. I've written them six letters, and four are just about gulls.'

interactables.name: Ruthwen Pinfold (Skeeton's stock runner)
pages: 'Stock runner! Socks to Apparel, kettles to Home & Hearth, and the odd lost child back to the service desk. Today's child was the same as yesterday's.'
'Skeeton's is round, so I never stop running. Nine laps before lunch. They cut Dov's job in the spring, so I run his route too. He sends postcards of his marrows.'

pages.text: 'Mulch in the stockroom? Don't let anyone call him rubbish. He counts socks better than the ledger does. I hang a dry towel over his corner when it rains.'

interactables.name: Odo Fairweather (garden sketcher)
pages: 'Shh. I'm sketching the fig. The fig moves when you're not looking. I need it to stop, or I need to stop looking away, and I've tried both.'
'I've drawn every plant out here. The bromeliads by the goblin statue keep coming out with a little glint in the moss. Odd.'
'Fifteen years I drew seed catalogues for a grain merchant. Every turnip, life-size. Then he bought a printing press. Now I do postcards of the fig, and I'm still trying to...'

interactables.name: Bettany Rinse (Suds & Duds & Beyond)
pages: 'I fold. Socks, trousers, soap. Yes, you can fold soap. You just have to believe, and have warm hands.'
'Wendell does the talking and I do the folding. He calls it synergy. I call it the reason I said yes to the job.'
'Twelve years on the presses at a strait hotel before this. You learn to fold a sheet in the steam with your eyes shut. I still dream in corners.'

interactables.name: Ulfrida Brask (Chain Row cook)
pages: 'Chain Row! Eight chains, one row, one cook covering the breaks. That's me. I can make all of it. Badly, but fast.'
'Furious Freja's is my favourite. Big portions, angry spices. I shout EAT! because it says so in the training manual, page one, in red.'
'My gran's stew beats all eight menus. I'm not allowed to make it here. Some days a pinch of her paprika ends up in Whet's soup, and nobody's complained yet.'

stock.name: Furious Freja Dumplings
stock.desc: Angry spices. EAT!

stock.name: Whet Sea Soup
stock.desc: Clams, kelp and a great deal of sea, to the training manual's gram. Ulfrida's gran made it better.

stock.name: Carna Skewer
stock.desc: A very serious sausage.

stock.name: Clara's Brews Cosy Cocoa
stock.desc: No grog before a brawl. OK, cocoa.

stock.name: Goo to Go Cup
stock.desc: Fruit goo in a cup. It holds its shape for a while, then it doesn't. EAT!

stock.name: Grab Grass Free-Range Salad
stock.desc: The grass roamed freely.

interactables.name: A Familiar Flower
pages: Between the ferns, something catches your eye. Oh! It's one of your favourite plants. You'd know it anywhere.

prompt.ask: What is it called, and what's special about it?

interactables.name: A Toy in the Gift Window
pages: In Beauty & Gifts, on the very top shelf: a toy you've wanted for AGES. You'd forgotten until right now. Hello, old friend.

prompt.ask: What is the toy, and why did you always want one?

interactables.name: A Tune on the Wind
pages: The busker's accordion wanders off his shanty and into a tune you can't shake. You've been humming it all week.

prompt.ask: What's the song called, and how does it go?

interactables.name: Pip Pinchbeck (age 6)
pages: 'I'm not sticky. The BABY is sticky. I'm just a bit sticky. On the hands.'
'When I grow up I'm gonna go down the chute WITH a sword. Mum says over her dead body. Dot says that means no. Dot doesn't know everything.'
'My dad is on a boat. A kelp boat. He can see us from the sea. I wave at ALL the boats so I don't miss him.'

interactables.name: Dot Pinchbeck (age 9)
pages: 'I'm in charge of Pip. Pip is in charge of nothing. Mum's in charge of the baby, and the baby's in charge of Mum.'
'I've tried every stall in the food court. Pixieats is best. You need thirty tarts, but they're tiny, so you get to try every flavour.'
'When I'm big I'll write the guide to the whole mall, with stars. Sweeny's gets four. Chain Row gets one, but the cook looks tired and it isn't her fault.'

interactables.name: Tobble Tumbletoe (age 10)
pages: 'That's my little brother. He's going to punch a mall. I'm going to referee it. Tweeeet! You have to say the tweet when you haven't got a whistle.'
'I know every shortcut in the Stem. There are none. It's a straight corridor. I checked a LOT. Then I checked with my eyes shut and walked into a planter.'
'Mum's on a double shift, so I'm in charge of my brother till the lamps change. I've got his snack, his spare sock and a list of rules. He's broken four.'

interactables.name: Wilf Puddingstone (age 8)
pages: 'Mum's choosing a rug. Dad's on the bench. I'm hiding in the round bit. It goes round FOREVER. I've been round eleven times and I never found the end.'
'I found a mannequin called Clive. He winked. Mannequins can't wink. He did though. I'm going to stare at him till he does it again.'
'There's a big bird with a badge by the rugs. His name's Marmaduke and he's a guard. I asked if I could be a guard too. He said HONK. I think that's yes.'

interactables.name: Marlo Seabright (age 5)
pages: 'I can't reach the telescope. Can you lift me? No? Can you be my telescope? What can you see? Is there a whale? Say there's a whale.'
'My gran says the sea is in my blood. I checked when I fell over. It's just blood.'
'Gran's having a pie. She said ten minutes. That was ages ago. That was a hundred minutes.'

interactables.name: Fen Larkspur (age 8)
pages: 'I threw a copper in the fountain and wished for a PikPik. Then I wished the PikPik would be nice. I've got two wishes going. Gran says that's greedy.'
'Gran knows everybody down here. Everybody knows Gran. I know the fountain. If you put your ear on the side it goes blub.'
'There's a PikPik in the round shop upstairs with a BADGE on. Gran says he's not for sale. I wasn't going to buy him. I was going to ask him.'

interactables.name: Clementine Rushwater (superfan, 14)
pages: 'Poppy does the glitter. I do the maths. We're going to win the superfan prize. There isn't one yet, so I've drafted the rules. There are fourteen.'
'I keep a tally of every point scored this season. In a notebook, with stickers, colour-coded by mall. Dad kept the harbour tallies for twenty years. I'm faster.'
'Honest question: when you go down and the ref picks you up, does the point still count against you? The rulebook's vague. I wrote to Goolax. They sent a sticker.'

interactables.name: Isolde Marrow (crystal fan, 15)
pages: 'My mum says crystals are just rocks. Mum is a stonemason. She's a ROCK person. She doesn't GET it. Rocks are what crystals are stuck inside.'
'I'm saving for the big geode. I have four coppers. It's a lot of coppers away. I sweep Mum's yard for them. She pays in coppers and advice.'
'The pixie at T.R.A.S.H. lets me hold the amethyst for five minutes if I'm careful. It hums. Mum says that's the leyline. Mum ruins everything.'

interactables.name: Plum (a wild PikPik)
pages: A very dark teal bird with a long neck and a huge fan tail stares at you with one big round eye. It has clearly forgotten why it came here.
The PikPik tilts its head. Then the other way. Then honks, softly, at a fern. A little tag on its leg reads PLUM. Somebody loves this bird.
On the back of the tag, scratched small: IF FOUND, SHE KNOWS HER WAY HOME. SHE DOES NOT. PLEASE JUST GIVE HER A NICE DAY.

interactables.name: Sir Wobbleneck (a wild PikPik)
pages: A PikPik with a pink crest standing straight up, like it's just heard terrible news. The gardeners call him Sir Wobbleneck. He hears the terrible news fresh every morning.
He looks at the koi. The koi look at him. Nobody is sure who is supposed to be scared. A gardener's chalkboard nearby reads: DAYS OF STANDOFF: 412.
A baby PikPik is asleep in the shade of his tail. He stands perfectly still, crest trembling, so as not to wake her.

interactables.name: Thimble (a baby PikPik)
pages: A baby PikPik, all fluff, legs and one enormous eye. It peeps. It falls over. It peeps about falling over, then gets up and does the whole thing again with total commitment.
Fern the gardener has put a little sign by it: THIMBLE. DO NOT FEED BREAD. SHE WILL EXPLODE WITH JOY. Underneath, smaller: SHE HAS NOT EXPLODED YET. LET'S KEEP IT THAT WAY.
Thimble follows Sir Wobbleneck everywhere, one step behind. He pretends not to notice. He has never once walked faster than she can.

interactables.name: Biscuit (a saddled PikPik)
pages: A big saddled PikPik with a brown leather saddle and a tag: BISCUIT. She's tied to nothing. She stays anyway, looking baffled, as if staying was someone else's idea.
Biscuit honks at the founder's statue. The statue does not honk back. Biscuit seems hurt, and then, a moment later, to have forgotten the statue entirely.
The saddle is old and oiled with care. Stitched under the pommel in faded thread is a second name: MARIT. Biscuit noses it when she thinks nobody's watching.

interactables.name: Gusty (a lost PikPik)
pages: How did a PikPik get down to the Dining Balcony? Nobody knows. Gusty doesn't know. Gusty is eating a napkin.
The gulls are furious about Gusty. Gusty has not noticed the gulls. Gusty has noticed your chips.
Gusty has found a patch of sun by the railing and sat in it. For one whole minute it is the calmest thing in the food court. Then a gull lands.

interactables.name: Marmaduke (a PikPik in Skeeton's)
pages: A PikPik is standing in Home & Hearth, staring at a rug with total confusion. A staff badge on its harness: MARMADUKE, SECURITY (UNPAID).
Marmaduke followed a shopper up the root stair one wet afternoon and simply never left. Skeeton's gave up. He gets a biscuit at closing.
A few of his tail feathers sit in a vase on the Beauty counter with a price tag. Marmaduke watches the vase from across the store with grave suspicion.

interactables.name: Halvard Crumbe (PikPik rider)
pages: 'That's Biscuit. Best PikPik on the strait. Took me fourteen years to teach her to stop. She still can't go.'
'PikPiks look lost because they ARE lost, always. Doesn't stop 'em getting where they're going. Took me forty years at sea to learn that trick.'
'Ban'ton's been riding PikPiks since before the strait had a name. Never once has a PikPik known the way home. Home's wherever the rider's standin'.'
'She was my sister's bird. Marit. The grey took her two winters back, and Biscuit stood at her door a week. Then she followed me. Been followin' since.'
brushoffs: 'Biscuit's still Biscuit. Lost as ever, lovely as ever. Ask me tomorrow.'
'You're makin' her nervous. She's always nervous, but now she's doin' it at you.'
'Biscuit, CHARGE! ...She won't. She never has. But you'd best go anyway.'

interactables.name: Feather Boa Rack
pages: FEATHER BOAS: 100% naturally shed PikPik tail feathers, teal-black with a pink shimmer. Very dramatic. Very Lorfida.
A tiny card: 'No PikPiks were plucked. They drop these everywhere. EVERYWHERE.'

interactables.name: Ada Quellbrook (visiting from Lorfida)
pages: 'We came for the arena and stayed for the PikPiks. My son has named nine of them. They are all, apparently, called Biscuit. He says the first one told him.'
'Back in Lorfida I lay stone for a living. Since Chard fell there's been a lot of stone to lay. This is the first week in nine years I haven't had dust in my teeth.'

interactables.name: Saffi Brightcap (Goolax promoter)
pages: 'Free sample! Goolax Original Fizz! Fizz the fight! Please take one, my tray is very heavy and very fizzy, and it's only half past ten.'
'I sang in a tavern band up in Banañon Town. Then the bard automatons came in, cheaper and never hoarse. Now I sing about fizz. It's still singing.'

interactables.name: Zibbit Coilwick (Crysto-Hut)
pages: 'Welcome to Crysto-Hut! Batteries, cables, crystal gizmos, and an adaptor for everything. If we don't have the adaptor, we have an adaptor for the adaptor.'
'Charge crystals: AA, AAA, and the big chunky ones that hum, for grown-up gizmos. Since the moon moved they hum flat at high moon. I sell them with a little note.'
'Before this I sorted screws on a factory line in Toggleton. Eleven years, one conveyor. That wall of tiny drawers holds three hundred and four kinds. I know every one by name.'
'People ask if I write the jingles, like the bard units. I do not. I once hummed a battery's part number and a customer clapped. Logged.'
brushoffs: 'Still browsing? I recounted drawer ninety while you stood there. Ninety is fine. Thank you for not asking.'
'You are now my longest-standing non-purchasing customer this week. There is no prize. I checked the stockroom.'
'SECURITY! ...The demo counter is beeping at you. It has never beeped at anyone before. Shoo, please.'

stock.name: Tinker's Tools
stock.desc: Everything a gadgeteer needs, in a roll-up case.

stock.name: Hooded Lantern
stock.desc: Bright light 30 ft, dim 30 more. Comes with a crystal wick.

stock.name: Pocket Glow-Lamp
stock.desc: A crystal that glows like a candle for 8 hours. Doesn't burn, doesn't drip.

stock.name: Crystal Battery (AA)
stock.desc: Powers small gizmos. Forty percent more glow!

stock.name: Charge Crystal (Chunky)
stock.desc: For grown-up gizmos. It hums.

stock.name: Cable Bundle
stock.desc: Three cables. Nobody knows what they connect. Everybody needs them.

stock.name: Adaptor for the Adaptor
stock.desc: Fits the adaptor that fits the thing.

stock.name: Crystal Shims & Coglets
stock.desc: A tin of tiny parts from drawers 112 to 140. Handy for artificer repairs. Zibbit can name every one.

stock.name: Clockwork Music Box
stock.desc: Plays one note very confidently.

stock.name: Thieves' Tools
stock.desc: 'For locksmith hobbyists.' Zibbit winks. His eyelid is a little brass shutter. It clicks.

stock.name: Grade I All-Purpose Tool (+1)
stock.desc: Artificers: +1 to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs, and it works as any artisan's tools. Zibbit tuned the crystal himself. It hums the Galleria jingle.

interactables.name: Wall of Tiny Drawers
pages: Hundreds of tiny drawers, floor to ceiling, labelled in tiny handwriting: CRYSTAL SHIMS. COGLETS. FUSES (SPICY). 'DO NOT OPEN: IT KNOWS'.
You open one at random. It holds exactly one screw and a note: 'you found him!'

interactables.name: Coach Ly'thol
pages: A glowing white orb hovers over the fighting pit, humming like a crowd about to roar. 'A contender! I'm Coach Ly'thol. I coach the Galleria team.'
'Well. I coach the WANTING. The part of you that leans forward when the buzzer's close. You do the rest.'
Ly'thol whirls around you in a ring of light. 'Drill one: the doorway. Every fight has a moment that opens like a door. Find it. Step through. Again! Faster! Lovely!'
'Drill two: the echo. Strike, then listen. The crowd knows what worked before your arm does. ...Hear that? The empty stands liked it.'
'Drill three: the stillness. Stand in the middle of the pit and want to win so hard the sand notices. There. You glowed a little. Take that with you.'
'Two creatures wanting the same thing, racing for it with everything they have. Is there anything sweeter in any world? I've never found it.'
'I wasn't always here, you know. I came over from the Feywild with a great band of pixies, after the Evanesceverance. A long, long flight.'
'I raced them the whole way. They say they won. I let them say it. Coaching starts with knowing when.'
Ly'thol dims to a soft glow. 'Every Selunemas I spend with Grivalba, an old ally of mine. Every single year.'
'It's the one day I don't want to win anything. ...Mostly. Don't tell her I said mostly.'
Ly'thol glows warm as a hearth. 'I've coached a lot of contenders. This team squabbles, sparkles and gets back up. Every time.'
'I'd cross worlds again for this lot. Don't tell the pixies.'

brushoffs: 'We've drilled enough for one week, contender. Rest is a drill too.'
'Go. Eat. Sleep. Come back hungry.'
'REFEREE! ...Dunstan, whistle this one off the sand. Kindly.'

interactables.name: Restroom Wall
pages: Scratched on the stall door: 'GALLERIA FOREVER'. Underneath: 'the hand dryer is stronger than our defence'. Underneath that: 'rude. true.'
A tiny pixie-height note by the basin: 'please lift me up to the mirror, I have a match later'.

interactables.name: Restroom Wall
pages: Pencilled on the tiles: 'carved into solid rock and STILL no extra sinks'. Someone has drawn one more sink. It doesn't work.
A neat sign: 'THIS WALL IS 400 YEARS OLD. PLEASE DO NOT TELL IT YOUR SECRETS. IT REPEATS THEM.'

interactables.name: Restroom Wall
pages: On the mirror, in soap: 'IF YOU CAME OUT OF THE CHUTE, YOU'RE DOING GREAT'. A drawn heart. A drawn soup bowl.
Graffiti by the dryer: 'Sweeny's pie review: 10/10. Bathroom review: also 10/10, I needed it.'

interactables.name: Bloop Marshworth (a mud-bubble Crud)
pages: A bubble of mud sits on a soggy log by the koi pond and burps politely. 'Bloop Marshworth. Drainage. I was born when the garden drain clogged. I'm very proud of the drain now.'
'Everyone asks if I'm related to Grab Bab the Bubble Boy. No. I did get his autograph when he ran for Magister in Cham'pew, though. It's a smudge. A beautiful smudge.'
'Before the drain I was a bit of the old bog up the hill, where the frogs were. They drained it for the road. I came out the other end, down here. Same mud. New job.'

interactables.name: Glossamy Drip (an oil-puddle Crud)
pages: A puddle of oil with two big blinking eyes. 'Glossamy Drip, railing polisher. A lamp-oil cart tipped on the cliff path one winter, and the bit that didn't go over was me.'
'Folk see a puddle and walk round it. I used to mind. Now I think of it as everyone giving me a little bow.'
'Sometimes I slide back up to the cliff path. There's a dark patch on the stones where I started. I sit in it and shine at the sea for a bit.'

interactables.name: Wheezle Fumehart (a smog-wisp Crud)
pages: A grumpy little cloud of grey smoke with eyebrows. 'Wheezle Fumehart. Smoke-alarm tester. Came out of an old grill vent when they knocked the kitchens through.'
'They put in extractor fans. EXTRACTOR fans. Do you know what that's like for a wisp? It's like a draught with ambitions.'
'I remember my vent. Brick. Warm. A crack where the sparrows sat. Now it's a wall with a menu on it. I go and sit by the menu.'

interactables.name: Rustle Binbright (a litter-tangle Crud)
pages: A rustling tangle of wrappers, ribbons and one Goolax cap. 'Rustle Binbright! Recycling volunteer! I sort the bins. Some folk say I AM the bins. I take it as a promotion.'
'Every wrapper has a story. That one's from tryouts. That one's from a very sad sandwich. That one has an address on it, and I'm working up the nerve to visit.'
'I was born on the old quay, the night after the last market before they paved it. Everybody went home and left their wrappers. I stayed. Somebody had to.'

interactables.name: Mulch Boxwell (a cardboard-lump Crud)
pages: A soggy lump of cardboard with a stamped face: THIS WAY UP. 'Mulch Boxwell. Stockroom. I came out of a wet delivery. Skeeton's gave me a job and a dry corner.'
'Please don't recycle me. I am on the payroll. I have a number. The number is on my back, I think. Can you check?'
'I remember being a shop. A little one, on the dock, before the storm took the roof. Then I was boxes. Now I am Mulch. It goes shop, boxes, Mulch.'

interactables.name: Gloria Jellicott (goo folk, visiting)
pages: A wobbly, cheerful blob of lime-green goo in a sun hat. 'Gloria Jellicott! On holiday! I've wobbled all the way from the coast to see this fountain.'
'I tossed in a coin and it floated right through me. Wish granted, I think? I wished to see it from the inside.'
'Thirty years I polished a lighthouse lens. Goo's wonderful on glass, no streaks. This is my first holiday ever, and I've decided to be very loud about it.'

interactables.name: Sprig (a walking sprout, garden volunteer)
pages: A sprout on two little root-legs, carrying a thimble of water. 'Sprig! Volunteer! I water the small plants. The big plants water ME, when it rains, by dripping. We take turns.'
'Fern says I'll grow up to be a fig one day. I hope not. The fig is rude. I want to be a fern, like Fern. She says that's not how it works. I'm going to try anyway.'
'I came here as a seed in a tourist's boot, all the way from somewhere with snow. I don't remember the snow. I think about it a lot.'

interactables.name: Prickla Saguarine (a cactus plantling)
pages: A small cactus in sunglasses, sunbathing on the balcony. 'Prickla. I'm on a desert holiday. This is a cliff. The sun can't tell the difference. With my eyes shut, neither can I.'
'No hugs. It's not personal. It's spines. People keep watering me as well. Three glasses of lemonade poured on me this week. One of them was nice.'
'Twenty years on an office windowsill. First they moved the desk, then they moved the window. I walked out after the window.'

interactables.name: B-0B "Bob" (mall-cleaning robot)
pages: A round little robot with a brush underneath and a bucket on top. 'GREETINGS. I AM B-0B. YOU MAY CALL ME BOB. I CLEAN. I HAVE CLEANED YOUR FOOTPRINT. YOU ARE WELCOME.'
'MY RIVAL IS THE MUD BUBBLE BY THE KOI POND. HE IS VERY NICE. HE IS ALSO MUD. I HAVE CLEANED HIM FORTY TIMES. HE RETURNS. HE SAYS HELLO.'
'FOUNTAIN COPPERS ARE COLLECTED ON THOUGHTSDAYS. DENTED COPPERS ARE RETAINED. THE ELDER GNOME LADY HAS APPROVED. CURRENT COUNT: ONE HUNDRED AND TWELVE.'

interactables.name: Marigold Fennwick (jingle fan)
pages: 'Every nine minutes, a brand new jingle. I haven't missed one in three years. My favourite was about pie. It was just the word pie.'
'I taught singing at the Banañon Town school for thirty-eight years. Children sing like that machine, you know: loud, honest, nothing in the middle. I find it restful.'

interactables.name: Tibbs Fennwick (age 6)
pages: 'Gran says I can go up and dance if the robot does the good one. The good one is ALL of them.'
'Mum and Dad work at the harbour all the time now, so I'm with Gran. Gran knows every song. Even the robot ones. Even the BAD robot ones.'

interactables.name: Corwen Ashby (heckler)
pages: 'I come here every lunch to heckle a jukebox with legs. Somebody has to keep it honest, and this lot just clap at everything.'
'Between you and me? The pie one was good. Don't tell it I said so.'
'Forty-one years crewing Seathern boats out of Ban'ton. My cousin in Quone calls the war a squabble. I call it what we called it on deck, and we don't talk at weddings.'

interactables.name: Juno Pettigrew (lunch break)
pages: 'Lunch and a show. The show is a robot shouting about food. The food is the show. I have forty minutes and I've timed them both.'
'I write the harbour tide tables. Since the moon moved they're wrong by a new amount every day, and captains shout at me. The robot shouts at everyone. I find that fair.'

interactables.name: Nettie Brack (goo folk, front row)
pages: A blob of pink goo wobbling in time with the beat. 'Front row! I wobble to the bass. It's the only way I know how to clap.'
'Bass goes in the bottom of me. Tune goes in the top. When it's a good one they meet in the middle and I go a bit purple.'

interactables.name: Oskar Vane (filming, 16)
pages: 'I'm streaming this on Twigtch. Eleven viewers. Twelve if Gran logs in. Say hi to Gran.'
'My break at Chain Row ended eleven minutes ago. The orc lady's covering for me. She covers for everyone. I'm going to owe her a Smite Shake.'

pages: A big 8-bit poster: MALL BRAWL 2026, WHERE EVERY TEAM HAILS FROM. A pin for each team, all over the map.
Someone has drawn a heart on Banañon Town.
