interactables.name: Basil Underleaf (420 Blaze It)
pages: A small leafy plantling in a knitted beanie waves a frond. 'Hey, friend. Basil. I water the moss, light the mushroom lamps, and keep the vibes at room temperature.'
'Sweet Grass for calm, Spice Grass for chat, and NAP for... well. You know. Take your time. Time's slower down here anyway.'
He hums, and the moss by your boots goes a shade greener. 'I was a cutting in a window box up in Banañon Town. Haven't seen the sea since. I hear it's big.'
brushoffs: 'Still here? That's cool. The moss likes company. I'm going to go and be quiet near it for a bit.'
'I've gotta water the lamps. I mean the moss. See? You're making me mix up my jobs, friend.'
'Gently, gently, out you float. The vibes need a rest, and so do my leaves.'

interactables.name: Maudie Gourdwhistle (puppeteer)
pages: 'Maudie Gourdwhistle. I do the voices, the hands and the tickets. My sister Brannie sews the puppets and does none of the talking.'
'I sang the ferry taverns for eleven years. Then the bard automatons came in: four hundred songs, no sandwich breaks. They still can't do hands.'
Kids are my best crowd. Grown-ups laugh at the jokes. Kids laugh when the puppet falls over, and the puppet falling over IS the joke.

0: 'First show of the season: Pootle Forgets the Way. One PikPik, one letter and the whole of Peel Lane. Pull up a chair.'
'My nephew Tobin sits at the front. He's seen it nine times. If he shouts out the ending, laugh anyway.'
1: 'Pootle's still on this week. I changed one line in the ferry scene. The snail in the second row will notice. He notices everything.'
2: 'This week: The Gardeners Who Stayed. My great-gran told me that one with two spoons and a turnip. I've upgraded.'
3: 'All of Banañon Town has brawl fever, so this week I gave them a brawl with fruit in it. Nobody gets hurt. Somebody gets peeled.'
4: 'Grumbald and the First Banañon. Someone tied a beard on his statue downstairs, so I wanted to give the puppet two. Brannie said no.'
5: 'Storm on the Strait is the quiet one. When the lighthouse comes on, the old fishers at the back go very still. I don't look at them.'
6: 'Last show of the season. Every puppet I own is in it. Brannie made D'fain a beard out of a mop head.'
'After today the booth sleeps till the thaw. I'll be singing at the ferry taverns on Seluday nights. Automatons can't take requests from old sailors.'

interactables.name: Tobin Gourdwhistle (age 7)
pages: 'Auntie Maudie's my auntie. I see every show first, because I sit under the booth when she practises.'
'Mum sews the puppets. She stabs her thumb and says a word I'm not allowed to say at the booth.'

0: 'Pootle gets to his granny's in the end. Don't tell anyone. I'm not telling anyone. I just told you.'
1: 'I've seen Pootle eleven times. I cried at the letter bit twice. The other times I was eating.'
2: 'The fairy lady says sorry at the end! ...Was that the end? Auntie Maudie says I'm a spoiler. I'm a goblin.'
3: 'Peely Dan slips on his own peel! Then he does it AGAIN! That's not spoiling, that's just true.'
4: 'Grumbald's real. He's downstairs. He's metal now. Auntie Maudie says that's what happens when you get famous.'
5: 'The storm one's a bit scary. I hold Minnow's hand for the thunder. She thinks it's for her.'
6: 'Next year Auntie Maudie says I can work the PikPik. I've been practising on my sock. My sock is very lost.'

interactables.name: Desmond Lumbridge (a regular)
pages: 'My lunch hour is sixty minutes. It takes me twenty-two to get here and twenty-two to get back. That leaves sixteen for puppets and a sandwich.'
'I clerk at the strait toll office. Eleven thousand ships stamped. Not one of them has stopped to watch a puppet show.'
'I review every show on Acorndr, out of five acorns. Nobody reads them except the puppeteer, who reads them out loud in a voice.'

0: 'Pootle Forgets the Way: four acorns. The ferry scene drags. The blue door made me feel something I haven't reported to my supervisor.'
1: 'Seen Pootle again. A line in the ferry scene is new, and better. I've gone up to four and a half acorns. She mustn't know I noticed.'
2: 'The Gardeners Who Stayed: five acorns. My family came over from Quone on a cabbage barge. The toll office is very dusty this week.'
3: 'THE BIG BANAÑON BRAWL: three acorns. Loud. The slip was coming from round one. I laughed anyway, and that goes in the review.'
4: 'Grumbald and the First Banañon. Historically doubtful. Four acorns, because I would also have bought the fruit.'
5: 'Storm on the Strait. No acorns. I don't give acorns to the ones that get me. I sat here for all sixteen minutes.'
6: 'Last show. I've taken the afternoon off, first time in nine years. My supervisor asked if I was ill. I said I had a booking.'

interactables.name: Minnow Fathomly (age 6)
pages: 'Grandad says the puppets are only socks with faces. Then how does Pootle know which way I'm sitting?'
'I'm going to be a fisher like Grandad. Or a PikPik. Whichever one lets me stay up later.'

0: 'Pootle got lost on the way to his granny's. I get lost on the way to my other granny's. She lives in Gok'Gok Harbor. That's very far.'
2: 'I would have gone with the goblins and planted the seed. I'm good at dirt. Ask my mum.'
3: 'I'm on Greenie's side. Green's my favourite colour. Also I'm green, so.'
5: 'Grandad went quiet at the storm show. I gave him my last sweet. He gave it back and said I need it more.'
6: 'I asked D'fain for a boat. A little one, for the bath. The big boats are Grandad's job.'

interactables.name: Abner Fathomly (retired fisher)
pages: 'Forty-one years fishing the strait. Now I sit here every Meluday and watch a goblin's hand pretend to be a bird. Best job I've had.'
'The tides have been daft since the moon moved. I'd have hated fishing this year. I'd have gone out anyway.'
That's my granddaughter at the front with her mouth open. She believes every word up there. Took me sixty years to stop believing things. No rush.

5: 'I got caught in a storm my second year out. A keeper on the point kept her lamp lit all night. Never thanked her. I'm thanking the puppet.'
6: 'She's asked D'fain for a little boat for the bath. I finished building it on Thoughtsday. Not a word, mind.'

interactables.name: Yarrow Rootley (in the queue)
pages: 'Oh, I'm not waiting for the show. I'm waiting. There's a difference. In a queue you know exactly where you stand.'
'Plantlings don't mind standing. I had roots for my first three years. This is luxury.'
'The seats are for people who haven't learned to love the waiting. I can hear every word from here.'

0: 'There's no queue yet. I'm the queue. Somebody has to start these things.'
2: 'Three weeks in line. A child asked what I'm queueing for. I said, "Yes." She seemed satisfied.'
4: 'A gnome asked if I was in the queue or just standing. I said both. She stood behind me. We're a queue of two now. I've never been happier.'
6: 'Last show of the season, and I'm at the front. I'm told the seats are free. ...I'll stand. I'd hate to lose my place.'

interactables.name: The Knucklebox
pages: THE KNUCKLEBOX. Hand puppets by Maudie Gourdwhistle, sewn by Brannie Gourdwhistle. A new show every week of the season.
Shows all day. Free. Children at the front, tall people at the back, snails wherever they've got to.

0: NOW SHOWING: POOTLE FORGETS THE WAY. A PikPik, a letter, and the whole of Peel Lane.
1: HELD OVER: POOTLE FORGETS THE WAY. Now with one new line. Can you spot it?
2: NOW SHOWING: THE GARDENERS WHO STAYED. A Banañon Town folk tale, with radishes.
3: NOW SHOWING: THE BIG BANAÑON BRAWL. Three rounds for the Golden Peel. Front row may get pulp.
4: NOW SHOWING: GRUMBALD AND THE FIRST BANAÑON. A true story, give or take a banañon.
5: NOW SHOWING: STORM ON THE STRAIT. Thunder by Brannie Gourdwhistle and a saucepan.
6: LAST SHOW OF THE SEASON: SELUNEMAS EVE ON PEEL LANE. Every puppet's in it. Back after the thaw.

lines: Somebody tracked arena sand all the way up to Skeeton's. Three floors of sand.
New rule: mop in straight lines. Faster, says the clipboard. The mop disagrees.
Glitter. Who brings glitter to a mall. I know who. The superfan.
Found a tooth by the root stair. Not mine. Hobb's got a whole jar of them out back.
They timed my mop breaks. Two minutes. My mop needs more than two minutes.
Twenty-two years. Used to know the regulars by their mess. New owners just see floor.

1: Tryouts. Foam fingers everywhere. I mopped up one the size of a dog.
4: Somebody's D'fain beard is shedding all over the Stem. Real wool. I'm saving the bits.
5: Six D'fains came through this morning. One of 'em tipped. I'll know his boots anywhere.

lines: Restrooms? West side, past the hat shop. Everyone asks. EVERYONE.
The map's upside down if you're standing on the cap. Most people aren't.
Four hundred and six 'where's the food court' today. It has not moved.
Lost child at the kiosk! No, wait. Lost parent. The child found me.
New directory came in. Smaller font. Rent went up, so the font went down.
My first week, a lady asked for a shop that closed years ago. It had been her husband's.

1: Tryouts done! Somebody left a whole cheer squad's worth of pom-poms here.
2: Back from Immia Beach! Directions to the food court: still down.

lines: I've drawn this mushroom eleven times. It's a different mushroom every time.
Do locals really eat banñons at every meal? I've had four today. I'm considering a fifth.
Postcard for Mum: 'Dear Mum, it is a mushroom. Do not send the Hall after me.'
Someone told me the cap was grown, not built. I've decided not to think about it.
Our malls back in Quone are flat. FLAT. Like animals.
First holiday in eleven years. I keep reaching for a rubber stamp that isn't there.

1: Came for a mushroom, stayed for tryouts. I screamed at a stranger. We're pen pals now.
6: I've extended my holiday for the whole season. Mum thinks I've joined the mushroom.
I've stopped drawing the cap. I draw the people under it now. Much harder to get right.

lines: I counted the steps to the food court. I got to a hundred and then I got hungry.
That man draws the mushroom with a face. I looked all over the mushroom. No face.
If you spin round in the plaza eleven times, the plaza spins back.
My tooth is wobbly. I'm gonna lose it in a brawl. A pretend brawl. With my brother.
Gulls are just pigeons that went to the beach and never came back.
The kiosk lady says the food court is below up. I'm still working on it.

0: Tryouts are on the ninth! I'm gonna try out. Mum says I'm too seven.
4: I'm asking D'fain for a brawl belt. And a pony. A brawl pony.
5: My tooth came out! It's under my pillow for D'fain. He's not the tooth one. I'm trying.
1: I watched tryouts on Tobble's shoulders. I screamed so loud my tooth wobbled more.

lines: Every sock bathed in our own soap before it ever meets a foot!
Soap-in-a-cardigan, next season, if the mill in Gok'Gok ever answers my letters.
Rent's up again, so we're adding a fourth ampersand: Suds & Duds & Beyond &.
The lavender line comes with matching pyjamas, so you can sleep inside the smell.
Mum's laundry had one sign: WE DON'T JUDGE STAINS. I brought the sign with me.

lines.text: Look who's browsing a shop with TROUSERS in it.
The boss said be polite if you came in, so I'm being polite at you very hard.
Our soap doesn't sulk. Can't say that about every shop on the Stem.
Two soap shops on one Stem. The boss checks your window before she checks ours.

1: Brawl special! Arena stains out in one wash, or the trousers are half price!

lines: Knit one, purl one, curse the gulls, repeat to the hem.
Pull the wrong thread on that cable-knit and ye've bought a scarf.
Want a hat that stays on in a strait gale? Chin strap. I'll sew ye a second.
The intercom sang about my oilskins. Rhymed 'waterproof' with 'roof.'
Sold a sou'wester to a brawler. Said it was for the rain of blows. I let him have it.
Red sky this morning. Old Dorrin by the koi saw it too. Neither of us said a word.

4: Selunemas jumpers in! D'fain on the front, a gull on the back. Gull's festive too.
5: Knitting my brother's Selunemas jumper. He's not coming home. It'll keep a year.

lines: Left fin's a nine, right fin's a ten. Most folk don't know that about themselves.
Got a pair of boots so quiet you can sneak up on yourself.
No, we don't sell the one boot. Unless you're a pirate. Are you a pirate?
Squeak test, every pair. A good squeak is how you know a boot's honest.
Cousin Sludd Wennoc sells sandals in Flot. Sandals! Toes out, in public!
Six years since I was home in Flot. I still lace my boots the Flot way.

2: Merfolk team next? You can't sell boots to a tail. I've been sketching anyway.
5: Made my first tail-boot. It's more of a sock, really. A merfolk lady bought two.

lines: That colour is you. No, not that one. That one is a cry for help.
Pearls are just a clam's little grudges. Wear them proudly.
North-wall rent costs more now than the reef I grow on.
Aura Fist wore a coral collar on Acorndr once. I still don't know who sent it.
That one I kept. First gown I ever cut. It fits no one, and I can't sell it.
A coral-pink brawl leotard. Stretchy, luminous, and it will never be clean again.

2: Did you SEE the Broad Squad's gowns? I've sketched all week. I'm inspired. I'm furious.
3: Since Lorfida, everyone wants sequins on their armour. I've stopped arguing. I sew.
5: A Selunemas gown for whoever wins the final. Measured for nobody. I'll take it in.

lines: I sniff every bar before it goes on the shelf. Once for scent. Once for honesty.
Eleven soaps in my bathroom and not one pair of trousers. As it should be.
My coworker wears black head to toe and her soap smells like a meadow. Respect.
I don't trust a soap that comes with ironing instructions.
Mopsy says socks fall out of soap. Socks do not FALL OUT of SOAP.
Gran's hands cracked every winter from lye. I put cream in everything I make.

5: Thirty-one bars of Selunemas soap, wrapped, one per person I know. They'll be SO clean.

lines: Don't rush me. I'm not slow. I'm thorough.
That's a mermaid's comb, or possibly a fish skeleton, and either way it's twelve silver.
A Toggleton fellow tried to haggle. I've been haggling since his grandad was a gear.
People ask if I'm related to that snail team. Different shell. Different slime.
My mother's shell had a blue spiral in it. I've looked on every coast for another.

5: The bottled drizzle snowed this morning. For Selunemas, I think, though it won't say.

lines: Saving for the axe that hums. I've got enough for the hum. Not the axe.
Head first or feet first down the chute? Asking for my dignity.
Fellow came out the bottom attuned to a spoon. He'd bought a sword.
My cousin wants a rematch with the chute. The chute hasn't agreed.
Mum gave me a whetstone when I left home. Haven't got a blade for it yet.

2: The Lorfida queens fight with fans, I hear. What beats a fan? A bigger fan?

lines: Shake before drinking. Not the pot. The pot does not like shaking.
*snaps* Steam goes pink when a pot's happy, grey when it isn't. That one's grey.
Healing, hiccup cure, and one that makes your hair briefly heroic.
Returns policy: if the pot's empty, so is the refund.
A hobgoblin just bought nine rain potions. He's going to be a weather system.
Read the label. Please. I write small because the pots are small, not to hide things.

3: Panto next? Theatre elementals, I hear. Burn salve's two for one this week.

lines: My knees creak like the root stair. And the stair's younger.
A gull stole my sandwich in '84. I've forgiven him. I haven't forgotten him.
Young folk walk so fast. Where are you going? It's a mall. It'll still be here.
They put a time limit on the benches upstairs. Not this one. This one knows me.
Dorrin brings tea down on Thoughtsdays. We don't talk. It's the best talk I get.

0: Tryouts on the ninth. I'll be watching. From here. With my ears.
6: Season's over. Mall's still here. Bench is still here. So am I. Good.

lines: I glued a tiny foam finger to my big foam finger, so now it points at itself.
I've got a stats chart on my wall. Mum calls it a shrine. It's a CHART.
Would the brawlers sign my forehead? Not forever. Like, until Seluday.
I watched the snail team's stream on Twigtch for six hours and they moved four feet.
My sign got forty-two acorns on Acorndr. Violet Ray Sky got forty thousand for a sandwich.
Did you SEE the new one on our team? Claws AND a pipe. I'm making a sign.

lines.text: Goolax turned down Aura Fist's rider. The PRISON DADDIES clause. I've started a petition.

0: Tryouts on the ninth! I've been practising screaming. Into a pillow. Mum asked.
6: Season's over? No. NO. What do I do with my hands now?

lines: No ticket? Then you're a spectator of the gate. It's a lovely gate.
Confiscated today: a lute, three air horns, and a very small catapult.
The stands fill from the top down. Nobody knows why.
Doug from the cheer squad keeps lifting me. I did not ask to be lifted.
Wind's off the cliff today. Hold your foam finger tight. I can't go after it.
New one on the team came by. Claws and a pipe. Pipe's fine. Claws, I'm watching.

6: Gate's shut till next season. I'll stand here a bit anyway. Feels wrong not to.

lines: New whistle. Goolax issue, little G on it. Tweets in tune. I miss my tin one.
Rule one: no biting. Rule two: no biting the ref. Rule three is mostly about biting.
A good ref sees everything. A great ref sees everything and pretends he didn't.
*points sternly at a sandbag* 'Yellow card. Don't make me get the red one.'
Not one brawler stayed down this season. I touch the whistle every morning for that.

1: Tryouts were clean, apart from somebody biting a sandbag. I've written the sandbag up.

lines: Found a gold tooth in the pit. Lost and found's got a whole jar of 'em now.
Raking spirals. Brawlers trip less on spirals, I reckon. Never asked one.
Word from upstairs: rake faster. I raked faster. Sand didn't care.
Morning sun comes over the strait and hits the pit first. Best five minutes I get.
The ref blew his whistle at my rake. My rake's never been offside in its life.

1: Tryouts left a crater by the north stand. Named it Gerald. Filling him in now.
6: Gerald's all filled in. Planted a bit of beach grass on top. Seemed right.

lines: Give me a C! Give me an L! Give me an IFF! ...It's a cheer about the cliff.
Pom-poms are hard when they're bigger than you. I'm a pom-pom with a pixie in it.
Doug says he can lift all three of us at once. Doug has said a lot of things.
Spirit fingers! No, more spirit. More fingers. MORE.
New cheer for the new one! Claws! Pipe! Unstoppable vibe!
Nobody cheered back last match. I cheered anyway. Somebody has to start.

0: Tryouts on the ninth! We'll cheer whoever makes it. ESPECIALLY the shy ones.

lines: Kelp crisps! Salty as the strait! Saltier! Legally I can't say saltier!
Foam fingers, one silver! Two silver for one that points the right way!
Prices up two copper. Not me. Upstairs. Blame the mushroom.
Banañon chips, still warm! From the sun! I left them in the sun!
Rook says he'll turn me round for one match this season. I'm holding him to it.

4: D'fain hats! Fits over a helmet! Fits over a second D'fain hat!
5: Selunemas gingerbread, half price! I ate the other halves!

lines: That moss took ten years. Please step around it. Not on it. AROUND it.
The fig dropped a fig on a tourist. On purpose. I've had words with the fig.
Mornings are best. Mist off the strait, dew on the ferns, nobody shouting.
Someone carved initials in the bamboo. By spring it had grown them out and kept the heart.
The owners want the hedges 'more efficient.' It's a hedge. It's very good at hedge.
The little sprout asks if it'll grow up to be a fig. I've told it there are worse fates.
Big koi's called Admiral. He's been promoted. He doesn't know.
Saw a three-master through the strait at dawn. Waved. They waved back.
My knee says rain. My knee's been right since I was forty.
Every ship in the world comes past this rock. Fifty years and I still count 'em.
My Ena's out past the point. Sea burial. You can see the spot from here.

4: Everyone's feeding Admiral Selunemas gingerbread. He's gone round.
5: Admiral can't fit under the lily pads now. Sits out in the open like a captain.

lines: Notebook? What notebook? It's a sketchbook. Of prices. Artistic prices.
Their fountain has fish near gears. I was unimpressed for three whole pages.
Their mall hums. Ours rustles. I grew up on a barley farm. I'll take rustling.
The leyline goes to Cogskill now. Fifty gold. My holidays are getting expensive.
Saw a Skeeton's buyer in Dullard's. I hid behind the kettles. She hid behind the toasters.
Mind the hatch. And the step. And the other step. The third one's the sneaky one.
Tube's humming nicely today. Hums higher when it's cold. Like me.
A Toggleton chap checked his pocket watch four times on arrival. Still late.
No snacks in the leyline. Last fellow took a pie. They're still finding pie.
Lovely down here. Dark, cosy, smells of rock. Best spot in the mall, for a mole.
High moon, the line runs warm. Never used to, before the moon shifted.
Tapped 'goodnight' down the line last night. Something tapped back. I think it's her.

6: Someone from the far end rode up the tube today. First time she's ever ridden it. I cried.

lines: Take a number. The number is seven. Everyone's seven. Nobody has complained about seven.
Gift-wrapping in three styles: neat, festive, and 'we tried'.
Lost property today: one boot, one sword, one grandad.
New owners, new forms. Same cap over our heads.
Exchanges on Thoughtsday. Complaints on Seluday. Gossip any day, quietly.
Toggleton buyers come in dressed as tourists. The good ones at least buy something.

6: Post-Selunemas returns desk is open. Brace. Brace. BRACE.
2: Glitter returns desk is open. We can't take the glitter back. Nobody can.

lines: Hold it to the light. Natural light. We haven't got any. Imagine it.
This tunic comes in black, darker black, and 'arena sand.' Arena sand is beige.
Fits in the fitting room but not at home? Our mirrors are kind. Yours at home isn't.
A brawler bought six identical shirts, 'one per contest.' I've put a seventh aside.
Twenty percent off everything! After the twenty percent on, but still. Off!
Rent went up, so the hems went up. The customers think it's fashion. I let them.

2: Since Lorfida everyone wants drag-queen sequins. We're out. I sew them on by hand now.

lines: I've been in fitting room four seven times today. For shopping reasons.
The Apparel lady keeps saying four is fine. Nobody calls a room 'fine' if it is.
I'm not loitering. I'm browsing very, very slowly.
This hat makes me look like a mushroom. In this mall that's camouflage.
My friend with the glitter sign says it's a portal. Portals don't have bass. Do they?
BREAK REMAINING: FOUR MINUTES. GROOVE REMAINING: INFINITE.
I HAVE COMPOSED A JINGLE NOBODY WILL HEAR. IT IS ALL BASS.
MY CHASSIS IS NOT RATED FOR THE WORM. I DO THE WORM.
IF ANYONE ASKS, I AM A COAT RACK.
TODAY'S JINGLE: 'GOOLAX, YOU'RE COVERED.' SUNG FORTY (40) TIMES. DANCED ZERO (0).
AT HIGH MOON MY CLOCK DRIFTS. LOGGED. I DANCE IN THE DRIFT.
Surf's up at the bottom of the cliff. Getting back up is the workout.
Brawl shields are just surfboards that tried harder.
Fellow wanted a fishing rod that fights. Sent him downstairs to Point and Chute.
Swell's all wrong since the moon moved. High tide turns up whenever it likes now.
Gent's been past my door four times looking for a big hat. I've started waving.
Life jackets half off. Not half the jacket. Half the price.

3: Since the merfolk match everyone wants flippers. Not one has asked where the sea is.

lines: That kettle's in B flat. That one's in a mood.
Downstairs they sell kettles that BEEP. A kettle should sing.
Round rugs for a round store! Square rugs for people who refuse to adapt!
A rug's where you'll drop your keys for the next twenty years. Choose well.
Hear that? I hummed an A and the copper one answered. Good girl.
That poor man on the bench has had three cups of my tea. I've stopped asking him.

3: Selunemas stock's in. D'fain mugs, his beard for a handle. Hold him by the chin.

lines: Spritz? Close your eyes. Breathe in. Open them. You're a meadow now.
I named one perfume 'Gull'. Four years, one sale. He came back to say it was perfect.
Free sample! It's smaller than me. If you drop it, we'll both be on our knees.
Gift sets in a shell. In a bigger shell. In a shell in a shell.
Feather boas in! PikPik tail, naturally shed. The donor watches them from the rug aisle.
Forty bottles a week, they said. I made one perfect one and had a lie down.

1: Arena scent's sold out again. I've been out on the cliff sniffing wet sand for refills.

lines: She's holding the blue rug now. The blue one's grey. They're both grey.
Ninety-one ceiling tiles. Ninety-two if you count the one with a gull on it.
If anyone asks, I've been helping. Morally.
My feet have filed a complaint. Skeeton's has a desk for that.
Bench is warm. Wife is happy. Kids are... somewhere.
Smells like proving dough round here. No, that's me. Eighteen years of nights.

4: Selunemas shopping. I've sat here so long a lady asked what I cost.
5: Bought the blue rug. Don't tell Mildred. It's for Selunemas. It's the same rug.

lines: Sea & Sport again. Hello, Sea & Sport. We meet again.
If I stand still, she'll walk round to me. It's a round store.
Towels! I heard 'towels!' ...No. That was a gull.
Gretta! GRETTA! ...Sorry. Wrong big hat.
I left a trail of crumbs. A child ate the trail.
We have towels at home, Gretta. We have eleven towels. I counted them for you.
My knees say sit. Gretta says knees are an excuse. I'll sit when I've found her.
Our escalator is a root. Theirs is a machine. Ours has character, and splinters.
Toggleton fashion: brass buttons on everything. Brass buttons on the buttons.
Don't mention Dullard's to the service desk gnome. He goes very quiet.
The leyline goes to Cogskill now. For research, I'd pay fifty gold. I did, actually.
Since the rent went up, I buy what sells. I used to buy what was lovely.
Goolax: you're covered! Sorry. They make us say it every hour.
Four hundred leaflets handed out. Three people read one. One person ate one.
Intern perks: free lanyard, free potion. The lanyard says PIPA. I've filled in a form.
I'm saving my free healing potions. For a really bad day. Or a paper cut.
Is it cold down here or is it the rock? It's the rock. It's always the rock.
Unpaid's just for now, they said. It's an investment. I wrote that down, to be sure.

lines.text: I'm not allowed to discuss Aura Fist's rider. I've been asked to 'source alternatives'.

lines: Moss is just carpet that's made peace with itself, man.
Someone asked if we sell glow mushrooms. Some of us ARE glow mushrooms.
Shop's quiet lately. Just me, the moss, and the drip.
Rent went up. The vibes didn't. Vibes are rent-controlled.
Time moves slower down here. That's not the grass, man. That's the rock.
The leafy one asked me to stop sporing on customers. It's like asking you not to blink.
North is that way. On the balcony, north is 'hold the railing'.
Compasses half price! They do north. The other directions are up to you.
A brawler wanted a map of the arena. It's a circle. I sold him a circle.
Every chart in here has Ban'ton in the middle. That's not bias. That's cartography.
The globe always sticks on Toggleton. Even the globe won't spin past it.
Loyalists want 'the Rebellion' on their charts. Rebels want 'the Squabble'. I print both.

2: Lorfida charts sold out. Fans, chiefly, and one very lost queen in full sequins.

lines: Worm of the day: Doris. Big girl. Wiggles with purpose.
Bait's live, lures are dead, nets are neutral.
No refunds on worms. Once they leave the tin, they're their own worms.
Smell? What smell? Oh. That's success, friend.
Kids keep asking if worms count as homologated gear. I'm looking into it.
The map lady next door bought me a candle. I said thank you. I think it was a message.
Three hundred coppers in since Alder passed. The cleaning bot keeps the dented ones.
Hear that drip? It was dripping when I was a girl. Same note.
My grandson brought me a sandwich. Cheese again. He's a good boy with one recipe.
My grandson says the shops are 'efficient' now. He says it the way you'd say 'damp'.
Sub-level folk work so hard. I bring biscuits now. They queue for the tin.
The plague took the colour from Alder's eyes first. This fountain's very blue, isn't it?

1: My grandson watched the tryouts on his break. Says his break was four minutes.

lines: Dusting! Every crystal, every day! The dust comes back! The dust LOVES me!
Rose quartz. For love. Or for holding down receipts, which is love if they're yours.
Don't touch the big geode. It's not cursed. It's just heavy, and I'm VERY small.
Staff discount? Of course! The staff discount is a hug. Non-negotiable.
Forty years of dew-on-a-stick in Ban'ton market. Crystals don't evaporate. Bliss!
Rent letter came this morning. I read it, I giggled, I put an amethyst on it.

4: Selunemas gift crystals! Wrapped by me, an hour each, so order early or order small!
5: Last Selunemas orders! My wings ache and the ribbon is winning. Order anyway!

lines: This one hums. Or my ears do. Either way, it's coming home with me.
Crystal under my pillow. Sleep's no better, but I wake with a very interesting cheek.
Twelve crystals and counting. My husband says it's a problem. I've put one on his side.
The pixie gave me a discount for 'good energy.' I DO have good energy. Ask my sister.
Thirty-one years married and he still can't tell rose quartz from a bar of soap.
Lean in. Closer. ...No, I've forgotten. It was good, though.
That busser downstairs has been mopping chute-soup all week. Poor lamb.
I don't gossip. I distribute information. Like a library, but louder.
The fountain granny's grandson works down here. She won't say where. I'll find out.
My husband's deaf as a post. Forty years of my best stories went straight into a pillow.

0: Who's trying out on the ninth? Half the food court, I hear. And a goth.

lines: Kelp on a stick! Stick on the side! Don't eat the stick. You can. Don't.
Gobble faster, there's a queue! It's one dwarf, but he's been in it since breakfast.
Voted best goblin in the food court! Only goblin in the food court. I did the vote.
Three goblin portions make one person portion. Or two hobgoblin snacks.
Banañon lady put banañon on my kelp. Customers loved it. I'm very cross about it.
Got a fork now. For the stick. Nobody's touched it. It's a lovely fork.

2: Lorfida special! Kelp on a stick with a sequin. The sequin's decoration. Stop eating it.
4: Selunemas kelp! Same kelp. I tied a bow on the stick and charged a copper more.

lines: Peel, pith, flesh, banañon. We waste nothing. The peels go back down to the terraces.
Our banañons grow on the terraces below town. Cliff-grown. You can taste the wind.
Someone asked for a dish without banañon. I sent them to Carna and didn't look back.
Fried, baked, mashed, sliced. Banañon is a lifestyle, darling.
Rent's up a third. Banañon's still two copper. Somebody eats that difference. Me.

1: We sold out after tryouts. Out of banañons. In BAN'TON. Brawlers, I tell you.

lines: Spicy up! Extra spicy up! Nope spicy... the cook's crying again.
Goo tip: blow on it, then wait. I never wait, but I haven't got a mouth to burn.
Grill's carved into the rock. Rock gets hot. Rock stays hot. Don't touch the rock.
Brawlers order nope spicy to look tough. Then they order milk. Milk's two silver.
Finish a NOPE skewer without milk and your name goes on the wall. The wall is empty.
Ribs? You get ribs. Salad? Herbivoracious is down the way. Coward.
The Brawler Platter has eleven meats. I'm working on twelve. Don't bring me a gull.
Cleaver's sharp, grill's hot, smile's free. Smile's extra on Seludays.
Chute folk land, smell the roast, and forget they ever bought a sword.
Mutton's up four coppers since spring. My platter's up one. Sit down and eat it.
Someone lit a candle. *a flick of his finger and it's out* Who keeps lighting candles.
Espresso, black. Grog, black. Mood, black. Napkins, sadly, white.
The jingle-bot wrote us a cheerful jingle. We play it backwards.
A goth girl runs a soap shop upstairs, I hear. A kindred spirit. I'll never say hi.
Violet Ray Sky's Tritone set is far too hopeful. I've played it every night this month.
Bards held Tritone with songs and barricades. Not automatons. Bards.
Petal on top! A petal on everything! Especially the petal tea.
Tiny forks! Tiny spoons! I lost one in a customer's beard last week. He's kept it there.
Grog Noire says we're too cheerful. I gave him a black petal. It's still on his counter.
Nectar tart for a big brawler? That's thirty tarts. Give me a minute.
Five people went red at me this week. None of them wrote the letter. I can tell.
By my oath, this smoothie shall be blended! ...The blender's stuck. Hold on.
Smite Shakes triple on contest days. People need courage. And potassium.
I swore to protect the innocent. Now I protect them from bad breakfasts.
Squire wanted. Must lift a blender. Must believe in fruit.
The order wrote again. They want the ceremonial mace back. I use it to crush ice.
Mind the steam! Pie's hot, oven's hot, I'm hot. It's a rock oven, dear.
Fish pie's got a whole fish in it. He's looking at you. That's freshness.
Mystery Pie Thoughtsday! The filling's a mystery today. Price is still a mystery too.
Everybody wants a pie for the long walk up the root stair.
Leftovers go down to the dock crews every Seluday, same as my gran did.

4: Selunemas mince pies! Same rock oven, same mystery price, extra raisins.
5: Last mince pies before the finale. Get one now; nobody gets near me after the chute.

lines: Salad's fresh. Fresh enough to argue back. Don't argue back.
Carnivores walk past me to Pleased to Meat. I watch them. I wait.
The Big Green has seven greens. One is just a very unripe banañon.
Kelp from the strait, ferns from the gardens, croutons from a man called Dorn.
Wilted? Not at my counter. *She taps a limp lettuce and it sits up straight.*
All seventeen stalls this month. Goo to Go five times. My doctor has the list.
New menu boards. Smaller print, bigger prices. Forty years a tax man. I notice.
Sit here long enough and the whole food court tells you its business.
My doctor says eat more greens. I've had the green goo. I've had the green pie.
The grill man and that little smoke cloud bicker like they've been married forty years.
Lunch break's thirty minutes now. Used to be forty. I miss those ten like a person.
Every time the intercom says 'Skeeton's' I flinch. Twenty-two years of flinching.
I'm not here. If anyone from upstairs asks, I'm a very still customer.
Thirty Pixieats tarts in twenty minutes. They're pixie-sized. Don't look at me like that.
A man returned a cloak today with a sword hole through it. He said it came like that.
Table for one. Best table. Nobody steals your chips.
Today's note under the corner table said 'BRING CAKE.' Romance, then. Or a cake spy.
Eating alone isn't sad. It's efficient. ...Oh no. I've caught it.
Pie, then roast, then a salad to say sorry to my stomach.
See the chisel slip on Sweeny's arch? Mine. Day my lad was born. Couldn't keep still.
Who's sticky? Why is the BABY sticky? He was in my arms the whole time!
Pip, put down the fork. Dot, put down Pip.
I grew up on forty acres of barley. Forty acres of quiet. I didn't know what I had.
One more go down the chute and we're going home. I've said that six times.
I'd give my left shoe for one hot meal sitting down. The baby's already got my right.
Table seven's had a spill. Table seven always has a spill. Table seven is cursed.
Somebody left a whole Brawler Platter. Just walked off. I'm not crying. Bit.
My mop's called Lady Sheen. She's seen things.
New sign says 'TWO-MINUTE TRAY TURNAROUND.' Nobody's told the trays.
Caught myself leaning at the skylight again. Somebody move table seven into the sun.
Incoming! Duck! ...False alarm. That was the jingle.
Fresh off the chute? Count your fingers. Good. Welcome to the food court.
Some land attuned. Some land confused. Some land holding someone else's lunch.
That rapier hums near pie. Can't sell it. It keeps wandering off to Sweeny's.
Upstairs sends a buyer down every few minutes. Like rain. Armed rain.
Fifteen years oiling cutlasses at sea. Nothing rusts down here. I oil them anyway.
♪ BUY. BUY. BUY. ♪ DRAFT FORTY-ONE. PROMISING.
COMPOSING... ♪ PIE IS A FOOD. ♪ COMPOSITION COMPLETE.
NEW DIRECTIVE: JINGLES MUST BE NINE SECONDS. I HAVE CUT THE BRIDGE.
I DETECT A HUMMING CUSTOMER. HUMMING IS UNLICENSED MUSIC. I WILL ALLOW IT.
QUERY: WHAT RHYMES WITH BANAÑON. ANSWER: NOTHING. I HAVE CHECKED EVERYTHING.
HECKLER PRESENT. 612 CONSECUTIVE LUNCHES. HE IS MY MOST LOYAL LISTENER.
This moustache is my real moustache. It's just on loan from itself.
The leyline goes to Cogskill now. I could go again. As a different gnome.
Toggleton gnomes wear goggles indoors. Page twelve, underlined, with a little drawing.
*adjusts moustache* Nobody saw me eat soup in this. Nobody.
If the team wants a scouting report, I have one. Nobody's asked. I've had it laminated.
Gok'Gok has gulls too. Theirs are greasy. Ours are merely rude.
My toaster wrote another poem: 'Bread. Hot. Done.' It's getting better.
A Cogskill tourist off the leyline asked where our gears were. I pointed at the cliff.
Wind's from the west. Hold your napkin. Hold your hair. Hold your nan.

3: Toaster poem for the merfolk match: 'Wet team. Dry bread. Good luck to all.'

lines: There goes Brian with a chip. Good for you, Brian.
Brian's nesting on the railing again. I've named the eggs. You can guess what.
Purple sails on the Wist boats now. The sailors wave. Nobody ever waved at a pilot.
Don't feed the Brians. They unionise.
Tides are an hour wrong since the moon moved. The ships mind. The Brians don't.
She laughed! At the gull. Not at me. Still counts.
Too soon to call it 'our table'? It's our table. I've decided.
I rehearsed a joke about the strait. It's a bit... straight. Oh no.
Do I order for both of us? Romantic or rude? The waiter won't tell me.
Mum wants a full report by teatime. With a drawing of the view.
Soup of the day: chowder. Soup of the wind: wherever it lands.
Table nine, hold your bread. Gull at three o'clock.
I carry soup along a cliff. Danger pay? Ha. Ha ha. No.
Every table's reserved for the view. The view's been booked since dawn.
Tide came in an hour early again. My uncle's nets are on the wrong side of the rock.
♪ Oh the strait is wide and the cliff is tall ♪ ...that's as far as I've got.
Tips in the hat, not the bellows. A copper got in once. Wheezed for a week.
The automatons wrote a shanty once. No sea in it. Just 'sea', forty times.
A gull requested a song. I played it. He left. Critics.
Busking permit's four silver a month now. Made three last month. Still here, aren't I?
Walk, don't run. If you're late, jog, but say sorry as you pass.
Same kid at the west planter, same moss. I've started saying good morning to both.
Clipboard says 'patrol briskly'. My knees outrank the clipboard.
Lost a glove? Crate by the restrooms. Somebody keeps putting a little hat on it.
Wrote down: 'goblin lady held the lift for a PikPik.' Best entry this week.

1: Since tryouts everyone walks like a brawler. Shoulders first, mostly into doors.
2: Team's back from Lorfida. Someone tracked glitter through my whole shift.

lines: Lamp nine's flickering. She does that when it rains up top.
A drop of sugar water and a glow-cap will shine all night.
That drip by the fountain's not a leak. That's the spire breathing.
Owners asked if the lamps could glow more efficiently. I asked the lamps.
Mind your head. Not for the ceiling. For the lamps. They bruise.
Old lady by the fountain sits under lamp forty. I keep that one bright for her.

1: Tryouts shook the whole rock. Three lamps fell over. I sat with 'em till they settled.

lines: Nine stalls and a whole row of chains. I need a second stomach.
Somebody just shot out of the ceiling holding a sword. Is that normal? Do I clap?
Four soups so far. All good. One was looking at me.
Which way's the balcony? I want to eat looking at boats.
Is it rude to sit with someone you don't know? At home it's rude not to.

2: Everyone's talking about Lorfida. I've never seen a drag show. I want to so badly.

lines: Coming through! Urgent kettles! Not hot. Just urgent.
Somebody put a sock in the ladle display. I'm starting to think it's personal.
Restock, restock, restock. The shelves eat faster than the food court.
The mannequins move at night. I chalked their feet. Every morning, a finger's width off.
Shoes last me six weeks in here. I buy them two at a time now, like bread.

1: Arena-wear sold out after tryouts. I folded the last shirt like a flag.

lines: Charcoal on my nose again, isn't it.
The koi won't hold a pose. I offered them bread. They hold it for bread.
Best light's when the mist comes off the strait. Nine minutes, on a good morning.
I drew a gull. A gull ate the drawing. Art criticism.
*blows on a smudge, and it lifts off the page as a tiny grey moth*
Forty trousers folded. Forty-one. Somebody unfolded one.
Smell that? That's laundered linen and ambition.
Wendell says every sock deserves a bath. I say every sock deserves a nap.
Price tags on the left leg. The hotel taught me that, and nobody ever said why.
My feet have walked more miles round this counter than I ever walked at sea level.

lines.text: Wendell, she's walking past. Be NICE. Fold something.
You look lovely today. Don't tell Wendell I said that.

lines: EAT! Sorry. Training manual.
Whet's soup is mostly sea. Today it's mostly sea AND a crab.
Clara's Brews says one grog before a brawl. I say one soup.
Eight menus, one hat. I've been meaning to wash the hat since Learn.
Sixteen breaks a shift, and I cover every one. Mine I spend standing in the freezer.
Is this soup? It's soup. I'm wearing soup.
I'm gonna be a brawler. Or a goblin. Whichever's louder.
That PikPik looked at me. I'm famous.
The smoothie dragon gave me a sticker. I'm a knight now. A sticky knight.
Pip, no. Pip, NO.
Thirty tarts is a normal amount of tarts.
Sweeny's fish pie: four stars. The fish looked at me. Minus one star.
Mum hasn't sat down since breakfast. I'm going to find her a chair.

2: Our team went to Lorfida and came back sparkly. Lorfida's going on my list.

lines: Tweeeet! That's a foul! On... you. Yes. I'm the ref, I decide.
I'm ten. That's double digits. I can go anywhere. Except the cliff.
My brother's going to punch a mall. I'm his coach.
When I grow up I'm being a ref. You get a whistle AND everyone has to listen.
My brother got scared of the big statue. I held his hand till he wasn't.

6: THE REF GAVE ME A WHISTLE. A real one. It's got a G on it. Tweeeeeeet!

lines: The round bit goes round FOREVER. I've been round three times.
Dad's asleep on the bench. Don't tell Mum.
Clive moved. I SAW him.
Mum says blue. Dad says it's the same rug. I think the rug wants to go home.
I'm hungry. I'm SO hungry. I had a biscuit but that was ages ago, like before.
Lift me up! I want to see the boats!
Gulls are just sky fish.
I've got a tooth wobbling. Gran says the sea will want it back.
The cactus lady said no hugs. So I hugged her shadow.
One copper, one wish. Two coppers, a PikPik. That's the rule.
The fountain gurgles back if you talk to it.
Gran says don't touch the lamps. I touched one. It was warm.
My other gran's not here any more. I throw her a copper too, in case.
Points so far this season: I have a chart. Want to see the chart? It's laminated.
Poppy's sign has more glitter than sign. I measured. Sixty to forty.
Superfans, assemble! It's just me and Poppy. Assembled.
Average brawl round: eleven minutes. Average chute queue: fifty-four.
Poppy cried at tryouts. I didn't. I wrote down the time she started, for her.

1: Tryouts! I counted every hit. Ninety-seven. Ninety-eight with the duck.
6: Final tally's done. One copy to Goolax. One copy to my dad, with stickers.

lines: That amethyst is calling my name. My name is also 'four coppers short'.
The pixie gave me a sticker. I'm keeping it forever.
Crystals don't DO anything. That's the point. They just ARE.
Five coppers now. Mum gave me one to stop talking about it. Lasted an hour.
SKRAWK?
*honks softly at a fern, then lowers her head to it*
*forgets mid-step which foot was next*
*fans her tail at her reflection in the koi pond*
HONK. ...honk?
SKRAWK?
*crest shoots straight up at a falling leaf*
*stares down a koi. The koi stares back.*
HONK. ...honk?
*holds very still so the baby PikPik can nap*
peep!
peep? *falls over*
*peeps at a leaf until the leaf moves*
PEEP.
*sits down in a footprint and fits exactly*
SKRAWK?
*turns to face her rider, then keeps turning*
HONK. ...honk?
*eats the thumb off a foam finger and looks very pleased*
*waits for her rider, very patiently, facing the wrong way*
*puts her whole head in a planter and holds very still*
SKRAWK?
*stares at a wall, deeply baffled*
HONK. ...honk?
*tries to eat a foam finger*
*steals a single chip and runs, enormously proud*
SKRAWK?
*stares at a wall, deeply baffled*
HONK. ...honk?
*tries to eat a foam finger*
*sits on a doormat that says WELCOME, as if it were an order*
*guards a single sock with total commitment*
Biscuit. BISCUIT. That's a planter.
Don't make eye contact. She'll follow you home. That's how I got her.
Feathers on my coat, feathers in my beard. Marit's coat was the same.
She's not lost. She's sightseein', and she's been at it eleven years.
Feed's up a copper a scoop since the new owners. She eats like a harbour.
Is every bird here this confused?
The gardens smell like rain that's been told a secret.
My feet hurt in the nicest way.
He asked if we could live here. I said the mushroom isn't taking lodgers. He asked it.
That's Biscuit number ten. No, love, you can't keep it. It has a home. Probably a home.
We spent the supper money on a foam finger. Supper is a banñon each and a lot of cheering.
Free fizz! Free fizz! Mind the bubbles!
Goolax: you're covered! ...I said that to a crying child earlier. He was, though.
Banañon Fizz, anyone? It tastes like a sunset off the cliff, if the sunset was sticky.
Two hundred samples to go before lunch. Have three. Have four. Please.
The little intern carries the tape, I carry the tray. We swap on Seludays.
Batteries! Crystal batteries! Forty percent more glow than last season's!
Cable for that? Cable for THAT? We've got a cable for everything except emotions.
Demo counter's beeping. High moon again. The coils don't like where the moon went.
Drawer two hundred and twelve: tiny left-handed screws. Six sold this year. Same customer.
Brawl season. Four crates of AAA for the light-up foam fingers, and it won't be enough.
A goblin once called me 'mate'. I replay it on slow afternoons.
Again! Faster! Lovelier!
The sand remembers every good fight. It's rooting for you.
No hands, so I clap with light. *flash flash*
Win or lose, you showed up. Showing up is the first point.
I can feel a rivalry brewing three floors down. Delicious.
Shoulders loose. Eyes bright. Want it. WANT it.
*bloop*
Drain's flowing lovely today. You're welcome.
Don't step on the log. The log is my office.
Mud is just soil having a feeling.
Rain tonight, I think. My bubbles go small before rain.
Mind the shine. That's me. Hello.
Every railing on this path, polished by yours truly. Lean on one. Go on.
I'm not a stain. I'm a SHEEN.
Rain thins me out. Wet days I sit under the fig and stay thick on purpose.
A gull tried to drink me once. We both learned something.
When the lamps come on I've got a little lamp in me too. Look closer.
*cough* That's not me. That's the grill. ...It's a bit me.
New extractor fan. I hate it. I respect it.
Alarm test! BEEP. They pay me in toast. Toast is smoke you can hold.
Raining on the balcony. Can't go out. I'd be fog. Fog hasn't got a job.
Recycle! Reuse! Re-me!
Found a Goolax cap. One more and I win a hat. I'll wear it on my other cap.
Don't litter. I've got enough relatives.
The kiosk lady saves me the good ones. Last week, a map with feelings. I sleep on it.
Shiny wrappers go to the oil puddle by the railings. She likes to see herself.
THIS WAY UP. I read it in the mirror once. It was backwards there. I worry.
Forty socks in. Thirty-nine socks out. I am looking inside myself.
Don't stand me in the rain. Rain is how I started. I don't want to start again.
Somebody called me rubbish. I am not rubbish. I am corrugated.
Wobble wobble! Lovely fountain!
Careful, I'm a bit runny in the heat.
I can see my lunch. So can you. Sorry.
Postcard to my sister: 'Saw the fountain. Was in the fountain. Weather fine.'
Watering! Watering! Mind your feet, I'm low!
Rain's coming. I can feel it in my leaves.
Hello, fern. Hello, fern. Hello, other fern.
I gave the baby PikPik a drink. She fell in the thimble.
I grew a whole new leaf on Thoughtsday. Fern clapped.
Sun's good. Wind's rude. Gulls are ruder.
No hugs. Spines.
I flowered once. Pink. Lasted a day. I think about it most afternoons.
Don't water me. I had a glass in early autumn. I'm fine till spring.
SWEEPING. SWEEPING. FOUND: ONE COPPER. FOUND: ONE TOOTH.
PLEASE STAND STILL. YOU ARE ON MY ROUTE.
BEEP. FLOOR IS NOW 4 PERCENT SHINIER.
THE NEW UNITS UPSTAIRS SING JINGLES. NOBODY HAS ASKED ME. I HAVE PREPARED ONE.
SUGGESTION BOX CONTAINED ONE SUGGESTION: 'BOB IS GOOD.' LOGGED. RETAINED.
Shh! He's composing!
Bravo! BRAVO! ...Was that the end?
Tibbs, sit up, he's starting. You may dance, but dance sitting down, dear.
Three thousand nine hundred and four jingles in my notebook. I'd like one slow one.
Do the pie one! DO THE PIE ONE!
I'm dancing sitting down.
Gran, he looked at me! The robot looked at me!
Gran, do robots have birthdays? I want to give him a hat.
BOO! ...No, that was decent. BOO anyway!
Rhyme something with banañon! Coward!
Nine seconds? I've had sneezes with more bridge.
Encore! ...I mean BOO. Encore-boo.
Retired three years. Flat's quiet as an empty hold. I come here for an argument.
*wobbles enthusiastically*
Louder! I want to feel it in my goo!
*wobbles the wrong way, then the right way*
Is this the pie one? I can't tell. I haven't got ears. I've got a feeling.
Chat says play the pie one.
Twelve viewers! New record!
Can you move? You're in my shot. Thanks.
Someone in chat wants Violet Ray Sky to cover the pie one. I want that so badly.
Moss is damp, lamps are glowing, all's well.
Breathe in. Breathe out. Slower. Slower than that. There you go.
Our new coworker's pipe smells like a campfire on a beach. Respect.
Rent went up. The moss didn't notice. Be like the moss.
No sun down here, so I take my break under lamp three. She's the warm one.

lines.say: Mopsy. MOPSY. There's a sock in the drain outside 101.
Psst. There's always a sock, love. I've forty in a bucket out back. Pairing them's my hobby now.
We sell soap. JUST soap. Not SOCKS.
Tell it to the drain, love.
Psst. You've been stood at that shelf an hour, love. I've had two breaks and a biscuit.
I'm restocking the lavender.
It's restocked. I watched you do it, heh.
I know. I'm savouring it.
If ANYONE from our shop makes the mall team, I'm making a commemorative bar. With their FACE in it.
Which soap shop, love? Heh.
Don't you DARE.
D'fain onesies. In the soap. In the SOAP, Mopsy.
Psst. Mopped up a D'fain beard this morning. Tiny one. I'm knitting it into something.
Don't KNIT the soap beard, Mopsy.
They've put a sign on the root stair. 'Keep moving. Every hour counts.'
Back in my day an hour on this bench was free. Still is. I've had sixty years of them, one at a time.
I don't think that's what the sign means, Fen.
My mother sat here when the mall was a cap and some shade. Nobody told HER to keep moving.
Remember when the cap was just a cap?
It's still a cap.
It's a cap with a shop in it. And a rent. And a letter about the rent.
And a directory with smaller writing.
Did you watch the tryouts?
From here. Heard every punch. Back in my day you could hear a pin drop at the... where was I?
You were telling me you didn't watch the tryouts.
I watched with my ears, Wim. My eyes were resting.
Grandkids want me to be D'fain this Selunemas. They've bought me a hat with bells on.
You've got the beard for it.
I've got a beard. It's not a beard FOR anything.
Okay, sign idea, are you ready? GALLERIA in glitter, a mushroom punching a gear, and the gear's crying.
Is the gear Toggleton?
The gear is ALWAYS Toggleton.
We're not scheduled against Toggleton. I've got the fixture list laminated.
YET.
My tryouts post got forty acorns on Acorndr, FORTY, do you know what that means?
Thirty-one were your gran. And it was a picture of your own ear.
My ear was AT the tryouts, Clem.
Did the Broad Squad really fight in heels?
In heels, on sand, in formation, and I've been practising in Mum's shoes, guess how THAT'S going?
You've fallen over eleven times since Seluday. I've been keeping a tally.
Badly. BEAUTIFULLY.
Where do you think the finale is?
Goolax won't say. Tilda at the kiosk doesn't know either, and she knows the drain schedule.
I've narrowed it down to 'somewhere', which is PROGRESS, Clem.
That's everywhere, Poppy. You've narrowed it down to the map.
I'm going down the chute one more time.
You've got a bandage on your bandage! They say the chute is SAFE AND FUN!
The chute and I have unfinished business.
What's attuning feel like?
Like a sneeze, but in your elbows.
And the second time? They say it gets EASIER!
Second time I landed in soup.
Since tryouts the queue's all brawlers.
Brawlers and US. They say every customer's a CHAMPION!
Then we're champions of the queue.
That's just standing, Harrow.
I'm getting you a Selunemas present. They say a blade is the gift that GIVES!
Not a weapon.
...A small weapon.
Then I have to take the CHUTE, Brannoc.
You blew the whistle at my rake.
*TWEEEET* Rule nine, friend. It was offside.
It's a rake.
It was an offside rake.
Sand's very flat today.
Thank you. I told it you'd notice.
Suspiciously flat.
It's called raking, Dunstan. Gerald's still lumpy, if you want something to look at.
Found a shoe in the pit after tryouts. Left one. I've put it in Gerald for safekeeping.
One of the hopefuls?
Might be the duck's.
The duck doesn't wear... does he?
That's the season, then.
I raked the sand into a little D'fain.
Leave him, friend. He's earned it.
Doug, lift! Five, six, seven, eight!
Lifting.
Higher!
This is the ceiling, Fizz.
New cheer: G! A! L! L! E! R!
Then what? I need the next beat!
I! A! Then everyone falls over.
I'm out of breath and I didn't even say it.
Once the team's picked we need a cheer with their names in! T-E-A-M!
We don't know their names.
So we leave a gap and shout really loud into it.
They've asked me to be the sleigh in the Selunemas cheer.
You'll be a WONDERFUL sleigh, Doug! S-L-E-I-G-H!
Who's D'fain?
All three of us. In one beard.
Where's the food court?
Down, love. Root stair, twelve steps, left at the koi.
Where's down?
...Below up.
Wow.
Is the mushroom alive?
It's a very old, very still mushroom.
So yes.
Ask your mum.
Can I work at the kiosk?
When you're older.
Where's the food court?
...You're hired.
Is that D'fain at the kiosk?
It's me in a beard, love. Kiosk policy from the first of the month.
Can D'fain tell me where the food court is?
Down. Ho ho ho.
Is that a Lorfida ship? The pink sails?
Eh? Glitter on the hull. Yes.
Do they always...
Always.
Admiral's eating well.
Someone's been feeding him banañon chips.
That someone is me. Ena used to feed the gulls. I feed the Admiral.
There's a leyline to Cogskill now. Fifty gold.
In my day we went to Toggleton with cannonballs.
You were the ship's cook, Dorrin.
I THREW the cannonballs. Ask anyone.
That Flot team was floating in the strait yesterday. Just floating.
Merfolk do that.
They waved at the koi.
Eh? Admiral didn't wave back. He's Ban'ton born.
Is it always this... green? And this much sky?
Most days, petal. You should smell it after rain.
Where are the gears?
We've got mushrooms instead. Fewer pinched fingers.
My ears are fizzing.
That's the leyline saying hello, petal. My well fizzed for a week when I found it.
Can it say goodbye?
Give it ten minutes.
Ride home's free. You paid both ways at your end.
Ban'ton pricing.
Same price both ends, petal. It's one tube.
...Fine. Where's the food court?
Down.
Are those Selunemas lanterns? Ours are steam-powered.
Ours are candles, petal. Beeswax, from the hives down by the old wells.
Quaint.
Warm, petal. The word you want is warm.
Horace, the blue or the grey?
They're the same rug. I've looked at both nine times.
They're different rugs, dear. One's blue. Look. Look.
Which one?
Take both home, dear. Try them in the hall. Go on. Go on.
Oh, could I? The hall's been bare since spring.
Please don't encourage the rugs.
You've been on that bench since lunch.
I've been supporting you. Since half past twelve.
From a bench.
From the BEST bench.
The D'fain teapot or the D'fain mug for Gran?
Both pour from the beard, dear. The mug just pours slower.
Then it's the same teapot.
Horace.
Sorry, have you seen my wife? Big hat? This is my fourth lap.
She was here a minute ago. Asking about you.
Which way did she go?
Round.
BERTRAM! TOWELS!
Gretta?! I'm HERE, love, by the... oars, I think.
She's gone round again.
Forty-one years. She's never once stood still.
Beach towels! Dries a whole goblin in one go!
She wants HAND towels. It says so here. Underlined, in her pen.
That's Home & Hearth.
Where's that?
...Round.
I'd like to return this hat.
What's wrong with it? Size, colour or regret?
It makes me look like the building.
We can do an exchange. For a different mushroom.
Is it Thoughtsday?
Chooseday.
Will you take a return on a Chooseday?
Choose another day.
I'd like to return a D'fain jumper.
Was it a gift, sir? Receipt, tags, or a note?
It was a threat. From my aunt. Look at his eyes.
Did you hear about the sword and the meat pie?
I STARTED that, dear. I distribute information.
Is it true?
It's true now.
The new owners sent a gnome with a tape measure round every bench on S1.
Measure them for what?
Efficiency, dear.
It's a bench, Ottilie.
That's what I SAID.
Anyone from down here trying out?
I hear the little pale fellow from the crystal shop might.
Him? He's lovely.
Lovely AND brave. Or lost. I'll know by Thoughtsday.
So what happened in Lorfida?
Depends who you ask, dear.
I'm asking you.
Then: SEQUINS. My niece in Lorfida posted me a whole envelope of them.
Which shop is your grandson at?
I'm not saying.
The bait shop?
...I'm not NOT saying.
Copper for the fountain?
What are you wishing for?
Longer lunch breaks. For the grandson. Alder always ate his lunch on that ledge.
That's a lot of coppers.
Someone's put lanterns in the fountain.
I ate one. Don't.
Why would I eat a lantern?
That's what I said beforehand.
Gran! Gran! Can I have a copper for the fountain?
You've had six.
This one's for a PikPik. A nice one. The other six were for practice.
Give the child a copper, Hettie. PikPik wishes are important.
WHEEEEEoof.
♪ A CUSTOMER HAS LANDED! THE CUSTOMER IS ON THE FLOOR! ♪
Am I attuned?
UNKNOWN. YOU ARE, HOWEVER, IN A JINGLE.
One more! I want to go one more time!
PURCHASE REQUIRED. ♪ BUY A BLADE, RIDE THE SLIDE ♪
That one's actually good.
A HUMAN WROTE IT. I AM STILL ANNOYED.
I came down with a sword AND a D'fain hat.
♪ SELUNEMAS! ♪
No verse? Nothing?
RHYMES ARE RATIONED UNTIL SELUNEMAS EVE. DIRECTIVE NINE.
I brought you a petal! Fresh off my finger.
I don't want a petal.
It's a BLACK petal.
...Leave it on the counter.
Your music is too happy. It comes through the wall.
Your music comes through the floor! I baked tarts to it. They came out sad.
Good. It's meant to sink.
Doing any Selunemas decorations?
One candle. Black. Unlit.
That's a stick, Corvin.
It's a festive stick.
Kelp on a stick! Two copper! Kelp on a stick!
Banañon on a stick, darling. Sweet, cliff-grown, picked Thoughtsday, two copper.
Kelp AND banañon on a stick, three! I thought of that! Just now!
...Are we partners now?
Twelve months, darling. Same special, same stick, same sign, same kelp.
It's consistent! It says so on the sign!
Your sign says 'Kelp On A Stik', darling.
Consistent spelling, too!
Did you get the memo? 'EVERY HOUR COUNTS.' They printed it on the back of our menus!
Mine's on the napkins, darling. And the cups, the till roll and the rent letter.
People are wiping their mouths with the motto, Marisol.
Rent's up a third. Let them wipe.
Another drink for the lady? Wind's up, so I'll fill it halfway. The gulls take the rest.
Just water. And the railing. I'll keep the railing.
I can hold the railing too. Should I? Is that... is that a thing we do?
Look, a ship! I read up on ships. In case. ...That's a big one.
Lovely. Don't point. Pointing makes me lean.
Right. I'll describe it instead.
This is our third date on a cliff.
Is that a lot? Mum says cliffs are romantic. Mum's never been up one.
Next time: food court. Underground. Walls.
Table by the pillar, under the stair, well clear of the chute. Safest seat in Town Banañon.
I got you a Selunemas present. I practised giving it. In the mirror. It went better in the mirror.
Is it a parachute?
...It's a scarf.
A long one? Long enough to tie to the railing?
Play something for the Brians. Brian on the post looks low today.
They walked out on the last one, love. Big Brian left in the second verse, and he's sat through the jingles.
Brian doesn't like anything, Barnaby. He liked my sandwich once. Two hundred years ago.
Then it's the shanty. Critics come round in the end. Took my wife eleven years.
Nine years on this shanty. One more verse to go.
What's it about?
A gull. Stole a captain's hat in a gale and wore it the whole way home to port.
Brian?
...It is now.
The Brians are wearing the hats I knitted.
How'd you manage that, love? I can't get a hat on my grandson and he's got hands.
I didn't. They took them off the stall. Brian has never once waited to be given anything.
Well. Best-dressed audience I've had since the bandstand.
Orsolya. Why is a board member dusting shelves?
Board of what, dear? The shelf board? She's ever so good with the shelf board.
Orichalcum. The lot who bought the Galleria. My cousin pours their tea. Tiny chair at the end.
Jynx? OUR Jynx? She told me she was 'in crystals.'
Shh. She's dusting this way. Look at a geode.
Everyone's moaning about the rent, dear. Jynx never does. She just hums and sells me rose quartz.
Course she hums. She sits on the owners' board.
Orichalcum's board? That pixie? She wraps my quartz in tissue paper!
Tiny chair, big vote. You didn't hear it from me.
Mopsy. There is a wet floor sign by the stair. I have checked the floor. It is dry.
Dry since Thoughtsday, love.
Then may I ask why the sign is out?
It likes the view.
Psst. You wrote me down on that clipboard. I saw. If it's about the timed breaks, I was timing them.
I wrote you under 'nice things people did'. It is a short list, so far. You are on it.
...What did I do?
You mopped round a sleeping child instead of over him. I thought somebody should write that down.
There is glitter on the stair and foam on all six benches.
And a whole tooth by the planter.
Tryouts, Mopsy.
Tryouts, Gantry.
Which lamp's the shy one?
Can't say. She'd know I told, and then she'd not glow for a month.
It's a mushroom, Pell.
Aye. And you're a lass with feelings, and nobody points at you.
Owners want the lamps on a timer.
Mushrooms don't do timers.
A timer don't know which one's tired. I wrote 'em that. In glow-ink, so they'd read it after closing.
First time? Rule one: people drop out of the chute. Look up.
Look up. Got it. Rule two?
Sweeny's pies, on a Thoughtsday.
I'm writing these down. And rule three?
Rule one again, but louder.
Do people really drop in from upstairs? Like, on purpose?
From Point and Chute. Buy a blade, take the slide.
And the soup?
The soup is a casualty.
Our team's back from Immia Beach.
How'd they do? Is it all right to ask? I don't know who our team is yet.
Depends who you ask. Everyone's got glitter on them, though.
Excuse me, where are the hand towels?
Home & Hearth, past Footwear, left at the candles, keep going round, can't stop, I've got Dov's route as well-
Which way round?
Either. That's the beauty of round.
Have you seen a mannequin with a name tag? Says CLIVE? He was in Menswear at seven, Hats by nine-
Mannequins don't have names.
This one's got a name tag, a new pose every morning, and my good scarf.
Folded forty trousers.
Washed, pressed & presented?
With our own soap.
Soap, suds & slacks. I'm putting that on a sign.
Bettany. Don't look. The JUST-soap one is walking past. The boss's words, not mine.
I'm looking.
I said DON'T look!
She looks great, Wendell.
...She does. Don't tell the boss.
Two free samples left. Should I offer her one?
Of OUR soap? To HER?
It's lavender.
...Fine. The small one. With a bow. And a card. And don't say it's from me.
Mum! MUM! Can we go down the chute?
We'd have to go UP first, Pip.
Then UP! Then DOWN! That's TWO goes!
Sit down. Eat your kelp.
Pip licked the table. I'm giving it one star.
It tasted like SOUP!
Pip! Tongue in, bottom down! ...Honestly, love, everything down here tastes of soup.
I want to be a brawler. Like the team that went to Lorfida.
You want to be an accountant.
A brawler who does accounts.
...I'll allow it.
Tobble! Watch me punch the statue! Three times! I counted!
Tweeeet! Foul! No punching founders!
He started it. He's holding a banañon at me.
Bet you can't find the mall cat. Rule is, no sandwiches.
Bet I can. She likes me. I checked.
Tweeeet! That's a sandwich in your pocket! Disqualified!
Can I ride her? Can I? Can I? I checked, I'm bigger than last week!
When you're taller'n her. Stand by her neck. Let's have a look at you.
I'm taller than her NECK.
SKRAWK. (Biscuit lowers her neck, just a bit.)
Halvard, love, your bird's been staring at my kiosk since ten past nine.
She thinks it's a nest.
It's an information kiosk.
Marit used to tie her up by a market stall. Reckon she's lookin' for her.
Morning, Tilda! Any wrappers for me? Any post?
Three. And a map someone cried on.
Ooh! Let's see. 'Food court, north stair, where ARE you, Gerald.' Poor Gerald.
Are you made of rubbish?
I'm made of LEFTOVERS. There's a difference.
What's the difference? I checked, you smell like a bin.
Confidence.
Barkley. *cough* Your grill's smoking.
That's you, Wheezle!
...Partly me. Mostly the NOPE skewers.
Want a skewer? Fresh off the rock! I'm only a bit runny today!
I'm a cloud, Barkley. I can't hold a skewer.
You could stand near it! Chow used to stand near everything I made!
...I'll stand near it.
♪ PIE. IS. A. FOOD. ♪ THANK YOU. I AM HERE ALL DAY. I AM BOLTED DOWN.
BOO!
YAY!
Both of those are applause, Tibbs. Mr Ashby just applauds in a lower key.
Rhyme something with banañon! Go on, you tin bandstand!
♪ BANAÑON. ...BANAÑON. ♪
Same word! My middle wobbled the same both times!
IT IS A PERFECT RHYME.

lures: Everybody tells the kiosk lady things. EVERYBODY. Want to hear?
Information desk! Directions, maps, and the odd juicy rumour.
The kiosk hears everything. Mostly 'where's the food court'. But not ONLY.

pages: 'A visitor from Lorfida swore the drag queen team's wigs are enchanted. Knock one off and the whole routine falls apart, she said. Then she winked.'
'I wrote it on a sticky note. The sticky note's on the kiosk now, so it's practically official.'
'A family off the Panto ferry told me about the No, But team. Genasi! Each one turns the floor around them into their element. Fire, water, rock, wind, lightning.'
'Inside their patch they've got the upper hand, and so do spells of that sort. So, and I tell everyone this: mind where you stand.'
'Moffidge folk keep asking me for directions. Their team, the Holy Rollers, has no captain, they say. They VOTE. Top of every round, they all pick one person.'
'Then everyone who hits that person adds the holy stuff. Crossbows, silver, holy water, extra radiant. If they pick your friend, protect your friend.'

lures: Psst. Things come up that tube besides passengers. Rumours, for one.
Hear all sorts at the hatch, petal. Want a bit of it?

pages: A Toggleton chap came up the tube swearing the Stalling team's market stalls are mimics. Toss one a coin, he said, and it bites its own side.
He'd had a fizzy ride, mind. I'd not lean on it.
A No, But fan rode up from Cogskill in a full fire-genasi costume. Tube's never fizzed like it. Swore blind they each carry their own element: fire, water, earth, air, lightning.
Wherever they stand, the ground goes that way, and they're strongest in it. Spells of the same sort too. I'd not pick a fight on their patch, me.
Fairrest Federation, rangers and druids, came through for a match. Two ways they play it: hang back in a firing line, or bury you in animals.
Most turn into the beast they already look like. One stays a person to do the spells. Break the line, go for the back. A mole's advice, that.

lures: OMG. Okay. I have INFO. Team info. Come here come here.
I know stuff! Brawl stuff! Ask me! Please ask me!
My chart has new bits. Do you want the new bits?

pages: 'Pocket Sand literally throw sand in your face. That's the whole team. Pockets. Of sand. I bought goggles for the front row AND a little broom.'
'Okay so The Broad Squad? Drag-queen MONKS. They fight in ROUTINES. Like choreography but punching.'
'When they stand close together they cover each other. Harder to hit, extra damage. Strongest together. So you'd have to split them up. Not that I WANT you to.'
'I've watched every Glorious Fiefdoms match on the scrying puddle and they CHEAT. They bunch up in a big huddle so the referee can't see the fouls.'
'If someone caught them and called it out really loud, like REF! REF! they could get disqualified. I've practised the yelling. Into a pillow.'
'The snail team! The Slymez! They're Snailsmen and they stream on Twigtch, and when viewers donate they get a LOOTBOX.'
'From the Cosmic Snailsmen Lootbox Service! Random magic battle items. Sometimes even LEGENDARY ones. Mid-fight! Six hours I watched. Worth it.'

lures: Customers talk while they try on fins. Want to hear what they said?
Gossip's free. So's my advice: never buy the yellow wetsuit.
A brawler tried on fins and told me things. Bare feet make people honest.

pages: 'Fella buying a snorkel swore the Blue Tsunami dry out on land. Ten minutes in an arena and they're flopping, he said.'
'I sold him a bucket too. And a second bucket, for the first bucket. Upselling.'
'Real talk from a guy who fought them: Blue Tsunami are all muscle. Barbarians, fighters, a couple of sneaky rogues.'
'They grab you, shove you, pin you. Keep your distance and guard whoever's squishy. He bought a lot of padding. All of it, actually.'
'Had a Fairrest ranger in for arrows. Smelled like pine. Said they either hang back in a firing line or swamp you with animals.'
'Most of them turn into the animal they already look like. One stays human for the spells. Rush the line, hit the back. Sprint shoes, aisle three.'

lures: Your table's ready. So is the gossip. Sit carefully.
Sailors tip in rumours. I've got a pocketful.

pages: 'A deckhand told me the No, But team are improv actors. Say no to them and they lose their powers. They must say yes, and.'
'He said it very confidently. He was also eating soup in a gale.'
'Sailors up from Sloppy Bottom Bay say Blue Tsunami fight like a riptide. All grabbing, shoving, pinning. Barbarians, fighters, a rogue or two.'
'Their advice, shouted over the wind: don't get close, and keep your soft ones behind you.'
'A fisher at table nine says the Fairrest Federation is secretly one very large bear in a long coat. Fifteen hats. One bear.'

lures: Sit, sit. I've got information. Distributed, not gossiped.
Ooh, you. Yes, you. Have I told you what the brawlers got up to?

pages: 'That snail team, the Slymez? Their shells are solid gold inside, dear. Crack one and it pays your rent. Mine went up, so I'm interested.'
'Those drag queens are a monks' order, you know. They fight in routines. Huddle close and they cover for each other: harder to hit, and they hit harder.'
'Pull them apart, I say. They're strongest together. A queen on her own is just a queen. Lovely, mind.'
'The B'dibom Bombs have the Holy Twins chanting. Two of them keep a chant going and it heals the whole team a little, every round.'
'Break the chant and two of them lose a whole turn starting it again. So hit hard and fast, dear. Little pokes just get chanted away.'

lures: Sit long enough and the food court tells you its business. Want some?
Lean in. Closer. Forty years a tax man; I know what people tuck away.
New week, new gossip. Same table, same chair, fresh crumbs.

pages: 'The Glorious Fiefdoms bring a herald who reads a proclamation before every fight. Twenty minutes, all titles. Bring a snack. Bring two.'
'That team Stalling fight from market stalls. Like this lot down here. Every round more vendors pour out. Flimsy, mind. One smack each.'
'They keep coming till you smash the stalls, and given time they build them back. Hit the source, I say. Same as the Goo to Go queue.'
'Heard Stalling hand out free samples mid-fight. Take one and you have to stop and review it. Five stars. Very binding.'

lures: Wipe, wipe, listen. You hear a lot under the tables.
Lady Sheen and me heard something. Want it?
Table seven's been talking again. Table seven never stops.

pages: 'Table seven says the B'dibom Bombs are actual bombs. Fuses and everything. I've got a mop ready, just in case.'
'Had a Pocket Sand student in, drawing runes on the floor. Burst ones, slow ones, push ones. Even a tiny guard rune that watched my mop.'
'Trick is, a rune that hasn't gone off yet, you can scuff it out. Lady Sheen did. Read the floor, and jog their elbow so they lose concentration.'
'Table four swears the Holy Rollers from Moffidge won't hit anyone holding garlic. Table four smells of garlic now. All of it.'
'Table two swears the Broad Squad glue their wigs on with honey, so gulls follow them into every arena. Bring your own gull, they said.'

bastionTidbits: Every MALL BRAWL match is scored on points and ends on a buzzer. Whoever's ahead when it goes wins the round. Simple. Loud.
The referee revives anyone who goes down. Nobody leaves the pit worse off than they came in, except their pride.
Every arena sets its own 'brawn and brilliance' challenges. Hitting hard helps. Thinking first helps more.
Each arena's objectives are announced a week ahead. Teams that read them early tend to win. Teams that don't, tend to read them after.
Only homologated gear is allowed in the pit: kit bought from approved merchants. Anything else waits at the gate until the buzzer.
Goolax covers every competitor's health insurance and hands out a package of healing potions each week. Brawlers argue about the flavours.
Every contest pays gold, and bracket winners earn Premium Vouchers. Brawlers guard vouchers like dragons guard gold, only shinier.
Sixteen mall teams share one standings board. Points from every contest add up, and the top-scoring teams meet at the end of the season.
At tryouts the top four make the team, and the judges and the coach each get one extra pick: a Judges' Favourite and a Coach's Pick.
Judges keep scorecards, three cushions and a bell. They love a clever play, but the buzzer doesn't care who looked good.
Galleria crowds fill the stands from the top down and stamp on a near miss. Visiting teams say the cliff wind makes it sound twice as loud.
Goolax's fizz fountain says GOOD LUCK, CHAMP on every pour. Superstitious brawlers drink exactly one cup before a match. Never two.
